paras.zh: “我们不能将我和普京进行比较。他是侵略者。他占领了我们。他杀害了成年人和儿童，还有他的士兵。他是一名恐怖分子，这就是为什么我希望特朗普总统能够非常明确地表达这一立场。”

paras.en: Trump reiterated his claim that Zelenskyy does not want the war on his country to end, saying on Truth Social that Kyiv was launching attacks on diesel refineries in Russia despite knowing it was “seriously hurting the world diesel markets”.
paras.zh: 特朗普重申了他的说法，即泽伦斯基不希望结束针对他的国家的战争，他在《真相社会》上表示，基辅正在对俄罗斯的柴油炼油厂发动袭击，尽管他知道这“严重损害了世界柴油市场”。

paras.en: “Zelenskyy doesn’t care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him… he doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did,” Trump wrote.
paras.zh: 特朗普写道：“坦率地说，泽伦斯基不在乎，欧洲向他提供了众所周知的所有资金……他不想结束这场战争，而且可能从来没有结束过。”

paras.en: Trump announced plans on October 9 for Russia to supply more than 300,000 metric tonnes of diesel to US and global markets to tackle fuel prices that have soared since the US and Israel launched war on Iran in late February. The move led Tehran to effectively close the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of global energy exports transited before the war.
paras.zh: 特朗普于10月9日宣布计划让俄罗斯向美国和全球市场供应超过30万吨柴油，以应对自美国和以色列2月底对伊朗发动战争以来燃油价格飙升的问题。此举导致德黑兰实际上关闭了霍尔木兹海峡，战前全球五分之一的能源出口是通过该海峡转运的。

paras.en: Trump’s embrace of Russian energy has angered not only Kyiv, but also European partners and many US officials, who say the move rewards Moscow while it continues its four-and-a-half-year war against Ukraine.
paras.zh: 特朗普对俄罗斯能源的拥抱不仅激怒了基辅，还激怒了欧洲伙伴和许多美国官员，他们表示，此举在莫斯科继续与乌克兰进行四年半的战争的同时，也给了莫斯科带来了回报。

paras.en: The Ukrainian president said on X on Sunday that he has spoken with US presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner as part of “virtually non-stop communication” between the two countries’ teams aimed at the “next steps in diplomacy”.
paras.zh: 乌克兰总统周日在 X 上表示，他已与美国总统特使史蒂夫·威特科夫和贾里德·库什纳进行了交谈，这是两国团队之间旨在“外交下一步行动”的“几乎不间断沟通”的一部分。

paras.en: “We are doing everything on our part to make this happen, and to ensure that America’s position is strong and helps bring peace closer. Peace that everyone, except Russia, has been waiting for over the past four and a half years,” Zelenskyy wrote.
paras.zh: “我们正在尽一切努力实现这一目标，并确保美国的强势地位并有助于实现和平。在过去的四年半里，除了俄罗斯之外，每个人都在等待和平，”泽连斯基写道。

paras.en: Zelenskyy spoke with Witkoff and Kushner as Russia and Ukraine continued to strike each other’s energy sites, with Moscow leaving thousands without power, and Kyiv carrying out the largest drone attack on Russia, in St Petersburg, since the war began.
paras.zh: 泽连斯基与维特科夫和库什纳进行了交谈，俄罗斯和乌克兰继续袭击彼此的能源基地，莫斯科导致数千人断电，基辅在圣彼得堡对俄罗斯进行了自战争开始以来最大规模的无人机袭击。

articles.title: Anthropic says it will commit 5% of shares to ‘public benefit’ fund

paras.en: Anthropic has pledged to commit 5 percent of its shares to a new fund dedicated to the public good, with plans to increase the contribution as the artificial intelligence giant’s market value grows.
paras.zh: Anthropic 承诺将其 5% 的股份投入到一个致力于公共利益的新基金中，并计划随着这家人工智能巨头市值的增长而增加捐款。

paras.en: The creator of the AI assistant Claude announced the new “Anthropic Public Benefit Fund” on Sunday as tech firms face intense scrutiny over the potential dangers posed by the frontier technology.
paras.zh: 人工智能助理的创始人克劳德周日宣布了新的“人类公益基金”，因为科技公司面临着对前沿技术带来的潜在危险的严格审查。

paras.en: In a blog post, Anthropic said it was committing 5 percent of company shares with immediate effect, subject to stockholder approval, with an additional 2 percent to be added “at the board’s discretion” for every 50 percent increase in the company’s value.
paras.zh: Anthropic 在一篇博客文章中表示，将立即投入 5% 的公司股份，但须经股东批准，并且公司价值每增加 50%，“董事会可酌情”追加 2% 的股份。

paras.en: “Because of the way the Fund is structured, the more Anthropic grows, the larger the share of the company that can be dedicated expressly to the public good,” the San Francisco-based firm said.
paras.zh: 这家总部位于旧金山的公司表示：“由于该基金的结构方式，Anthropic 的增长越多，公司可以明确致力于公共利益的份额就越大。”

paras.en: “It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives. We are instead directing that equity to the public benefit.”
paras.zh: “科技公司向高管提供不断增加的薪酬奖励是常见的做法。相反，我们将这些股权用于公共利益。”

paras.en: Anthropic said the fund could be used to make donations to traditional nonprofits, as well as “direct distributions to specific populations”.
paras.zh: Anthropic 表示，该基金可用于向传统非营利组织捐款，以及“直接分配给特定人群”。

paras.en: It said labour market disruption due to AI could be among the causes addressed by the fund.
paras.zh: 该基金表示，人工智能造成的劳动力市场混乱可能是该基金解决的原因之一。

paras.en: “Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed,” the company said.
paras.zh: 该公司表示：“Anthropic 已经投入 2 亿美元来研究和解决这个问题，但考虑到人工智能的进步速度，可能需要更大胆的方法。”

paras.en: “The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.”
paras.zh: “该基金将拥有多种能力来追求这些目标。”

paras.en: Anthropic, officially registered as a “public benefit corporation” in the US state of Delaware, said the fund would not be used for lobbying or political donations, either in the United States or overseas.
paras.zh: Anthropic 在美国特拉华州正式注册为“公益公司”，表示该基金不会用于在美国或海外进行游说或政治捐赠。

paras.en: Founded in 2021 by former employees of ChatGPT creator OpenAI, Anthropic is preparing for what could be the largest public initial offering in history. It is expected to list on the US stock market before the end of 2026, with analysts forecasting a valuation exceeding $2 trillion.
paras.zh: Anthropic 由 ChatGPT 创建者 OpenAI 的前员工于 2021 年创立，目前正在为可能是历史上最大规模的公开首次公开募股做准备。预计2026年底前在美股上市，分析师预测估值将超过2万亿美元。

paras.en: The company’s charter requires its leadership to balance shareholder returns with responsible AI development.
paras.zh: 该公司的章程要求其领导层平衡股东回报与负责任的人工智能开发。

paras.en: The breakneck speed of AI development has prompted widespread anxiety about possible negative downstream effects on society, including the job market.
paras.zh: 人工智能的惊人发展速度引发了人们对可能对社会（包括就业市场）可能产生的负面下游影响的普遍担忧。

paras.en: In a report published last month, consulting firm McKinsey estimated that up to 11 million American workers may need to switch careers over the next decade due to AI-driven automation.
paras.zh: 在上个月发布的一份报告中，咨询公司麦肯锡估计，由于人工智能驱动的自动化，未来十年可能有多达 1100 万美国工人需要转换职业。

articles.title: Lula and Bolsonaro spar in Brazil’s fiery first presidential run-off debate

paras.en: Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro fired off a barrage of personal attacks during their first debate a week before a tight presidential run-off.
paras.zh: 巴西总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦和右翼参议员弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗在紧张的总统决选一周前的首次辩论中发起了一系列人身攻击。

paras.en: In a chaotic exchange on Sunday, the two men called each other “liar” multiple times, accused each other of corruption, dragged up various scandals, and clashed on issues from public security to healthcare.
paras.zh: 在周日的混乱交锋中，两人多次互骂对方“骗子”，互相指责对方腐败，牵扯出各种丑闻，并在从公共安全到医疗保健等问题上发生冲突。

paras.en: Lula said Bolsonaro was “a habitual liar” and a “thug”, and physically distanced himself on stage from the candidate he called a “militiaman”, alluding to his alleged ties to Rio de Janeiro’s paramilitary groups.
paras.zh: 卢拉表示，博尔索纳罗是“惯于说谎的人”和“暴徒”，并在台上与他称为“民兵”的候选人保持身体距离，暗指他与里约热内卢准军事组织的所谓关系。

paras.en: Bolsonaro, who led the first-round election with 47 percent to Lula’s 45 percent, said it was better to keep Lula at a distance “because my wallet could be stolen”.
paras.zh: 博尔索纳罗在第一轮选举中以 47% 的支持率领先卢拉 45%，他表示最好与卢拉保持距离，“因为我的钱包可能会被偷”。

paras.en: Throughout the debate, Bolsonaro, 45, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, paced behind Lula, shaking his head, smirking and scoffing as his adversary spoke.
paras.zh: 在整个辩论过程中，45 岁的博尔索纳罗（前总统雅伊尔·博尔索纳罗的儿子）在卢拉身后踱步，在对手发言时摇头、傻笑和嘲笑。

paras.en: The 80-year-old Lula, who is seeking a fourth term, demanded an explanation regarding a corruption investigation involving the older Bolsonaro, a question his opponent dodged.
paras.zh: 正在寻求第四个任期的 80 岁卢拉要求就涉及老博尔索纳罗的腐败调查做出解释，但他的对手回避了这个问题。

paras.en: The younger Bolsonaro responded by calling Lula a “clown”, and then parried by bringing up a potential corruption case involving one of the president’s sons.
paras.zh: 年轻的博尔索纳罗回应称卢拉是“小丑”，然后提出了涉及总统儿子之一的潜在腐败案件来回避。

paras.en: Jair Bolsonaro has been under house arrest while serving a 27-year sentence connected to efforts to overturn the 2022 election, which he lost to Lula.
paras.zh: 雅伊尔·博尔索纳罗 (Jair Bolsonaro) 因推翻 2022 年选举而被判 27 年徒刑，在服刑期间一直被软禁，但他在选举中输给了卢拉。

paras.en: Cost of living, public spending in focus
paras.zh: 生活成本、公共支出成为焦点

paras.en: Flavio Bolsonaro hammered away at the top concerns of Brazilians, such as the cost of living and crime, and accused Lula of “reckless spending” to get re-elected, referring to various social measures the president has announced during the campaign.
paras.zh: 弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗重点阐述了巴西人最关心的问题，例如生活成本和犯罪，并指责卢拉为了连任而“不计后果地花钱”，并提到了总统在竞选期间宣布的各种社会措施。

paras.en: Lula countered by asking Bolsonaro about his plans to emulate the drastic public spending cuts implemented by Argentina’s right-wing president, Javier Milei.
paras.zh: 卢拉反驳道，他向博尔索纳罗询问他效仿阿根廷右翼总统哈维尔·米雷实施的大幅公共支出削减的计划。

paras.en: Bolsonaro dodged the question throughout the debate and pivoted to different topics.
paras.zh: 博尔索纳罗在整个辩论中回避了这个问题，并转向了不同的话题。

paras.en: When his father’s handling of the COVID-19 pandemic came up, Bolsonaro admitted that this “wasn’t an area where we saw the best results during Bolsonaro’s presidency. I’ll offer a mea culpa here.”
paras.zh: 当谈到他父亲对 COVID-19 大流行的处理时，博尔索纳罗承认，“这不是我们在博尔索纳罗担任总统期间看到的最好结果的领域。我在这里表示歉意。”

paras.en: Lula also sought to portray his opponent as out of touch with poor Brazilians, saying Bolsonaro had never used the country’s public healthcare system or taken a bus.
paras.zh: 卢拉还试图将他的对手描绘成与贫穷的巴西人脱节，称博尔索纳罗从未使用过该国的公共医疗系统或乘坐过公共汽车。

paras.en: “My opponent only knows about buses from books. He has never even stepped foot on one. He has no idea what the world of work is like,” Lula said.
paras.zh: “我的对手只从书本上了解公共汽车。他甚至从未踏过公共汽车。他不知道工作世界是什么样的，”卢拉说。

paras.en: Ahead of Sunday’s debate, supporters of each candidate gathered en masse in public to show their allegiance.
paras.zh: 在周日的辩论之前，每位候选人的支持者在公共场合聚集在一起以表达他们的忠诚。

paras.en: Pro-Bolsonaro crowds wearing Brazil’s national colours of yellow, green and blue packed Paulista Avenue in Sao Paulo’s financial centre, where the candidate addressed the crowd.
paras.zh: 圣保罗金融中心的保利斯塔大街挤满了身着巴西国色黄、绿、蓝的支持博尔索纳罗的人群，这位候选人在那里向人群发表了讲话。

paras.en: Lula supporters wearing red, symbolic of his Workers’ Party, filled Brasilia’s plaza of government buildings, while students backing the president protested against Bolsonaro in Rio de Janeiro.
paras.zh: 卢拉的支持者穿着象征其工人党的红色衣服，挤满了巴西利亚的政府大楼广场，而支持总统的学生则在里约热内卢抗议博尔索纳罗。

paras.en: “We need the current government to remain in power. If another government comes in, we’re, excuse my language, screwed,” said Lula supporter Sonia Maria at the Brasilia rally.
paras.zh: “我们需要现任政府继续掌权。如果另一个政府上台，请原谅我的语言，我们就完蛋了，”卢拉的支持者索尼娅·玛丽亚在巴西利亚集会上表示。

paras.en: “I don’t like bandits. Out with Lula!” said Bolsonaro backer Vera de Sousa in Sao Paulo.
paras.zh: “我不喜欢强盗。跟卢拉一起出去吧！”博尔索纳罗的支持者维拉·德索萨在圣保罗说道。

paras.en: Also on Sunday, Brazil’s federal police asked the country’s Supreme Court to open an investigation into Bolsonaro over a money laundering accusation involving a lawyer close to him.
paras.zh: 同样在周日，巴西联邦警察要求该国最高法院对博尔索纳罗展开调查，调查涉及一名与他关系密切的律师的洗钱指控。

paras.en: The presidential candidate is already under investigation for his links to Daniel Vorcaro, a disgraced former banker who financed a movie about Jair Bolsonaro’s life.
paras.zh: 这位总统候选人已经因与丹尼尔·沃卡罗(Daniel Vorcaro)的联系而受到调查，丹尼尔·沃卡罗是一位名誉扫地的前银行家，他资助了一部讲述贾尔·博尔索纳罗一生的电影。

paras.en: Lula spent 580 days in prison in 2018 and 2019 on a corruption conviction that was later annulled over flaws in the investigation and legal proceedings.
paras.zh: 卢拉在 2018 年和 2019 年因腐败定罪而入狱 580 天，后来因调查和法律程序中的缺陷而被撤销。

paras.en: Polls suggest a close race for the October 25 run-off, with Flavio Bolsonaro holding a slight advantage after finishing nearly 2 percentage points ahead of Lula in the first round on October 4.
paras.zh: 民意调查显示，10 月 25 日决选的角逐势均力敌，弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗 (Flavio Bolsonaro) 在 10 月 4 日第一轮投票中领先卢拉近 2 个百分点，略微领先。

paras.en: Both candidates hope to engage the 33 million voters who stayed home in the first round, equal to about one in five eligible voters.
paras.zh: 两位候选人都希望吸引第一轮投票中留在家里的 3300 万选民，相当于合格选民的五分之一左右。

paras.en: Sunday’s debate was the first between Lula and Bolsonaro after the candidates both declined previous opportunities. A second debate is scheduled for October 23, just ahead of the run-off.
paras.zh: 周日的辩论是卢拉和博尔索纳罗候选人都拒绝了之前的机会后举行的第一场辩论。第二次辩论定于 10 月 23 日举行，即决选之前。

articles.title: Ukraine and the U.S. are at odds over Starshield. Here's what to know
articles.author: Kristin Wright

paras.en: Ukraine and the U.S. are at odds over Starshield. Here's what to know
paras.zh: 乌克兰和美国在“星盾”问题上存在分歧。这是你需要知道的

paras.en: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and U.S. officials remain at odds over disruptions to a key satellite communications service used by the Ukrainian military.
paras.zh: 乌克兰总统泽伦斯基和美国官员在乌克兰军方使用的一项关键卫星通信服务中断问题上仍存在分歧。

paras.en: Zelenskyy told NBC's Meet the Press on Sunday he believes the U.S. government is behind his military's loss of normal access to the Starshield and Starlink services, claiming tech firm SpaceX imposed the restrictions in response to a "message from [the] American government."
paras.zh: 泽连斯基周日在 NBC 的“会见媒体”节目中表示，他认为美国政府是其军队无法正常使用星盾和星链服务的幕后黑手，并声称科技公司 SpaceX 实施这些限制是为了回应“美国政府的信息”。

paras.en: Warning that the U.S. siding with Russian President Vladimir Putin would be a "historic mistake," the Ukrainian leader claimed that the Starshield system has not been fully restored, despite what U.S. government officials have said publicly.
paras.zh: 这位乌克兰领导人警告说，美国站在俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京一边将是一个“历史性错误”，并声称尽管美国政府官员已公开表示，星盾系统尚未完全恢复。

paras.en: In a post on X over the weekend, Zelenskyy said the restrictions on the system have hindered Ukraine's ability to intercept weapons launched by Russia, calling the consequences "very painful and unpleasant."
paras.zh: 泽连斯基周末在 X 上发帖称，对该系统的限制阻碍了乌克兰拦截俄罗斯发射武器的能力，并称其后果“非常痛苦和不愉快”。

paras.en: The dispute comes after days of back and forth between Ukraine and the United States over the Starshield system.
paras.zh: 这场争端是在乌克兰和美国就星盾系统问题进行了数天的反复争执之后发生的。

paras.en: Starlink is a satellite internet network operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX to provide internet service to the U.S. and other counties. Since 2024, the U.S. Defense Department has shared a high-powered military version of the network called Starshield with Ukraine, which has cost the Pentagon billions of dollars.
paras.zh: Starlink 是由埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 SpaceX 运营的卫星互联网网络，为美国和其他国家提供互联网服务。自2024年以来，美国国防部与乌克兰共享了一个名为“星盾”的高性能军用网络，五角大楼为此花费了数十亿美元。

paras.en: Ukraine relies on the network in its defenses against Russia's nearly five-year full-scale war.
paras.zh: 乌克兰依靠网络来防御俄罗斯近五年的全面战争。

paras.en: "We use Starlink to intercept the jet fighters that are hitting our civilians and killing families," said Zelenskyy online. "We also use Starlink for middle strikes on enemy military targets in our temporarily occupied territories. We were unable to do this when there were restrictions. And the third, most important thing is people. Our soldiers, who have been on the front line for weeks and months, are being delivered food and water using appropriate drones with Starlink."
paras.zh: 泽连斯基在网上表示：“我们使用星链拦截攻击我们平民并杀害家人的喷气式战斗机。” “我们还使用星链对我们临时占领领土上的敌方军事目标进行中间打击。当有限制时，我们无法做到这一点。第三，也是最重要的是人员。我们的士兵已经在前线工作了数周和数月，他们正在使用星链适当的无人机运送食物和水。”

paras.en: Zelenskyy said the disruptions to Starshield came without warning last week. He told NPR in an interview that losing normal access to the critical defense network had left his military's frontlines vulnerable. On X over the weekend, he said the network's speed hasn't been fully restored.
paras.zh: 泽连斯基表示，星盾系统的干扰是在上周毫无预警的情况下发生的。他在接受美国公共广播电台采访时表示，失去对关键防御网络的正常访问使他的军队前线变得脆弱。周末X时，他表示网络速度尚未完全恢复。

paras.en: It's unclear why Ukraine has experienced restricted access to Starshield. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said on X that the U.S. government is responsible for the system, and that "any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS."
paras.zh: 目前还不清楚乌克兰为何对星盾的访问受到限制。 SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 在 X 上表示，美国政府对该系统负责，“对速度或使用的任何限制均由美国军方决定，最终由美国总统决定”。

paras.en: A bipartisan group of senators is calling on the Defense Department's inspector general to investigate how the system was disrupted.
paras.zh: 一个由两党参议员组成的小组正在呼吁国防部监察长调查该系统是如何被破坏的。

paras.en: Speaking to reporters on Friday, President Trump denied interfering with Starshield. "I don't know if it was anybody because it wasn't me, and I don't think it was Elon. And from what I understand, it's the same as it's always been," he said.
paras.zh: 特朗普总统周五在接受记者采访时否认干扰星盾计划。 “我不知道是不是任何人，因为不是我，我也不认为是埃隆。据我所知，情况和以前一样，”他说。

paras.en: Secretary of State Marco Rubio also rejected Zelenskyy's claims that the disruptions to the system were deliberate.
paras.zh: 国务卿马可·卢比奥也驳斥了泽连斯基关于系统中断是故意的说法。

paras.en: "It's just categorically false. No one at the White House ordered anyone to slow down internet or slow down speed so that certain drones couldn't use it," Rubio told reporters on Saturday, adding that Ukraine requested access to the system to carry out strikes deep inside Russia.
paras.zh: 卢比奥周六对记者表示：“这绝对是错误的。白宫没有人命令任何人减慢互联网速度或降低速度，以使某些无人机无法使用它。”他补充说，乌克兰要求访问该系统以对俄罗斯境内进行深入的打击。

paras.en: "That's under conversation. It's under discussion right now of how they would want to use it," he said.
paras.zh: “这正在讨论中。现在正在讨论他们希望如何使用它，”他说。

paras.en: The Starshield disruptions have renewed questions over the United States' commitment to supporting Ukraine against Russia's war, with tensions between President Trump and Zelenskyy growing over the past few days.
paras.zh: 过去几天，特朗普总统和泽连斯基之间的紧张关系不断加剧，“星盾”中断事件再次引发人们对美国是否承诺支持乌克兰对抗俄罗斯战争的质疑。

paras.en: Earlier this month, Trump moved to ease U.S. sanctions against Russia that had been passed by Congress. After Zelenskyy pushed back on the move, calling it a "weak decision by strong partners," Trump lashed out, criticizing Ukraine for striking Russian refineries, which he said was affecting U.S. diesel prices. "I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president," Trump said.
paras.zh: 本月早些时候，特朗普采取行动放松国会通过的美国对俄罗斯的制裁。在泽伦斯基回击此举，称其为“强大合作伙伴的软弱决定”后，特朗普猛烈抨击，批评乌克兰袭击俄罗斯炼油厂，称这影响了美国柴油价格。特朗普说：“我认为乌克兰是时候选出一位新总统了。”

paras.en: The war of words has continued in the past few days, with the Ukrainian president outlining further areas of disagreement. On Sunday's Meet the Press, Zelenskyy also said that U.S. intelligence sharing with Ukraine concerning Russia ballistic missile attacks was blocked for three days, but has resumed.
paras.zh: 过去几天，口水战仍在继续，乌克兰总统概述了进一步的分歧领域。泽连斯基在周日的会见媒体节目中还表示，美国与乌克兰有关俄罗斯弹道导弹袭击的情报共享被阻止了三天，但现已恢复。

paras.en: Ret. Navy Adm. Mark Montgomery told Here & Now's Scott Tong he believes the Starshield disruptions are a response by the White House to Zelenskyy's efforts to strike Russian oil refineries.
paras.zh: 退休。海军上将马克·蒙哥马利告诉《此时此刻》的斯科特·唐，他认为星盾干扰事件是白宫对泽伦斯基袭击俄罗斯炼油厂的回应。

paras.en: "This is really a signal. It's a signal to stop attacking oil refineries and President Zelenskyy has properly pushed back on that," Montgomery said. He added it's an extremely vulnerable moment for Ukraine, as more Russian drones are able to get through.
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利说：“这确实是一个信号。这是一个停止攻击炼油厂的信号，泽伦斯基总统已经适当地反击了这一信号。”他补充说，对于乌克兰来说，这是一个极其脆弱的时刻，因为更多的俄罗斯无人机能够通过。

paras.en: Zelenskyy said on Sunday that Russia has launched more than 4,000 strike drones, bombs and missiles against his country over the past week. Russian attacks on Saturday night targeted energy substations leaving tens of thousands of people without electricity, according to Zelenskyy.
paras.zh: 泽连斯基周日表示，过去一周，俄罗斯向俄罗斯发射了 4000 多架无人机、炸弹和导弹。泽连斯基表示，俄罗斯周六晚间针对变电站发动袭击，导致数万人断电。

paras.en: Ukraine has responded to Moscow's strikes with its own attacks on Russian oil refineries. Ukrainian forces hit a major refinery southeast of Moscow last Thursday after Zelenskyy had said he was "done" following Trump's calls for an "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine.
paras.zh: 乌克兰也对俄罗斯炼油厂发动袭击，以回应莫斯科的袭击。上周四，乌克兰军队袭击了莫斯科东南部的一家大型炼油厂，此前泽伦斯基表示，特朗普呼吁俄罗斯和乌克兰之间实现“能源停火”，他已经“完成”了。

paras.en: On Sunday, Ukrainian strikes set an oil export terminal and a depot on fire in the Russian city of St. Petersburg, as Kyiv launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia.
paras.zh: 周日，乌克兰的袭击导致俄罗斯圣彼得堡的一个石油出口码头和一个仓库着火，基辅向俄罗斯发射了 1000 多架无人机。

articles.title: 'Life is absolutely brutal in Gaza,' says World Food Programme head
articles.author: Michelle Aslam

paras.en: 'Life is absolutely brutal in Gaza,' says World Food Programme head
paras.zh: 世界粮食计划署负责人表示：“加沙的生活绝对残酷”

paras.en: The UN's World Food Programme says 1.4 million people in Gaza are suffering acute food shortages and that funding gaps are forcing cutbacks in critical aid, despite the U.S. brokered Hamas-Israel ceasefire.
paras.zh: 联合国世界粮食计划署表示，尽管美国斡旋哈马斯与以色列达成停火，但加沙仍有 140 万人面临严重粮食短缺，资金缺口迫使关键援助削减。

paras.en: It's been more than a year since famine was declared in parts of Gaza, and while some progress has been made to address food shortages there, humanitarian organizations are warning that progress is extremely fragile. Despite the Israel-Hamas ceasefire brokered by the U.S., more than two-thirds of Gaza's population - nearly 1.4 million people - are experiencing crisis levels of acute food insecurity. The U.N.'s World Food Programme says the approaching winter months will only increase the need for more humanitarian aid and more money to pay for it. Carl Skau is the acting executive director of the World Food Programme. He joins us now from Jerusalem. Welcome to the program.
paras.zh: 加沙部分地区宣布进入饥荒已经一年多了，虽然在解决那里的粮食短缺问题上取得了一些进展，但人道主义组织警告说，进展极其脆弱。尽管以色列和哈马斯在美国斡旋下停火，但加沙超过三分之二的人口（近 140 万人）正经历严重的粮食不安全危机。联合国世界粮食计划署表示，即将到来的冬季只会增加对更多人道主义援助和更多资金的需求。卡尔·斯考 (Carl Skau) 是世界粮食计划署代理执行主任。他现在从耶路撒冷加入我们。欢迎来到这个节目。

paras.en: CARL SKAU: Thank you. Thank you for having me on.
paras.zh: 卡尔·斯考： 谢谢。谢谢你邀请我参加。

paras.en: ROSE: You have just returned from a trip to Gaza. What did you see there?
paras.zh: 罗斯：你刚刚从加沙旅行回来。 What did you see there?

paras.en: SKAU: Well, this is my eighth trip to Gaza since the war, and it's a year into the ceasefire. You know, my takeaway is that not much have changed, frankly. There is - life is absolutely brutal in Gaza. There is no basic services. You know, there is massive destruction. There is no proper shelter. And frankly, the insecurity continues. We were at one of the distribution points - they told me there that someone had been killed the day before. As we were leaving, there had been shooting at the exit point. And so, you know, I think we record some average 50 security incidents per day. So, you know, we have been able to push back on famine, but that's much thanks to our efforts. We've been reaching almost every person in Gaza for the past few months, but that progress is fragile, and it can easily be reversed.
paras.zh: 斯考：嗯，这是我自战争以来第八次前往加沙，停火已经一年了。你知道，坦率地说，我的结论是没有太大变化。加沙的生活绝对是残酷的。没有基本的服务。你知道，那里有大规模的破坏。没有适当的庇护所。坦率地说，不安全感仍在继续。我们在一个分发点 - 他们告诉我前一天有人被杀。当我们离开时，出口处发生了枪击事件。因此，我认为我们平均每天记录大约 50 起安全事件。所以，你知道，我们已经能够遏制饥荒，但这很大程度上要归功于我们的努力。在过去的几个月里，我们几乎接触到了加沙的每一个人，但这种进展是脆弱的，而且很容易被逆转。

paras.en: ROSE: Can you tell us a little bit about who you met with there? And is there any, perhaps, a story that illustrates the food shortages that persist?
paras.zh: 罗斯：你能告诉我们一些你在那里见到了谁的情况吗？也许有什么故事可以说明持续存在的粮食短缺吗？

paras.en: SKAU: When I was at one of these distribution points where we serve hot meals - it's a big pot, and you share a meal for everyone who shows up with a pot to walk away. And these are the most vulnerable. These are the people that live close to the front line. They told me that many had been displaced or - you know, in the last few weeks. Already, they don't have cooking gas to cook for themselves. And, you know, they told me they eat once a day. They have no fresh vegetables. So these are people who, you know, are not eating enough already.
paras.zh: SKAU：当我在一个提供热饭菜的分发点时，这是一个大锅，你会为每个带着锅走开的人分享一顿饭。而这些人是最脆弱的。这些人住在靠近前线的地方。他们告诉我，许多人在过去几周内流离失所。他们已经没有燃气可以自己做饭了。而且，你知道，他们告诉我他们每天吃一次。他们没有新鲜蔬菜。所以，你知道，这些人已经吃得不够了。

paras.en: And as we are now facing the winter, we are being forced to cut. You know, we are cutting almost half a million people off assistance in these next few weeks. It's not because the needs are down. It's also not because we are not able to bring in food. It's because the funding is no longer there.
paras.zh: 由于我们现在正面临冬天，我们被迫减产。你知道，在接下来的几周内，我们将削减近 50 万人的援助。这并不是因为需求下降。这也不是因为我们不能带食物进来。因为资金已经没有了。

paras.en: ROSE: What happened? Why is the funding falling short of the need?
paras.zh: 罗斯：发生了什么事？资金为何无法满足需求？

paras.en: SKAU: Well, it's because it's a massive operation. You know, we've been reaching 2 million people every month in an environment that is also relatively expensive. So it's a massive undertaking. But of course, this is not the time to turn away. If anything, this is the time to step up. We need to sustain this effort, sustain this emergency support so we can protect the gains that we made.
paras.zh: SKAU：嗯，因为这是一项大规模的行动。您知道，我们每个月都在一个相对昂贵的环境中接触 200 万人。所以这是一项艰巨的任务。但当然，现在还不是转身离开的时候。如果有的话，现在是挺身而出的时候了。我们需要维持这一努力，维持这种紧急支持，以便我们能够保护我们取得的成果。

paras.en: But also, we need to move beyond that, frankly. I mean, we need to now really make a push on early recovery, help people get some proper housing and shelter before the winter. Then on the food side, you know, we want commercial to come in. We want the markets to start working so that we can instead distribute cash. It's much cheaper, and it helps people - you know, they can choose for themselves. There is some dignity in that, and it would be the way to start some kind of domestic food system as well.
paras.zh: 但坦率地说，我们还需要超越这一点。我的意思是，我们现在需要真正推动早期恢复，帮助人们在冬天之前获得适当的住房和庇护所。然后在食品方面，你知道，我们希望商业介入。我们希望市场开始运转，这样我们就可以分发现金。它便宜得多，而且对人们有帮助——你知道，他们可以自己选择。这有一定的尊严，而且这也是启动某种国内食品系统的方式。

paras.en: ROSE: I want to ask you about the flow of goods and supplies into Gaza. There has been some reporting about the suspension of commercial shipments into the Gaza Strip in recent days. What is going on there?
paras.zh: 罗斯：我想问你有关进入加沙的货物和物资流动情况。最近几天有一些关于暂停向加沙地带商业运输的报道。那里发生了什么事？

paras.en: SKAU: Well, that's deeply concerning. There is some disagreement around taxation for commercial goods. And, you know, this is at a time when, if anything, we need to scale up. When we were there, there hadn't been any entry of commercial goods for five days. We now saw some commercial trucks moving. I hope that means that this has been resolved because what we really need is to expand the commercial and bring more fresh foods and vegetables.
paras.zh: SKAU：嗯，这非常令人担忧。关于商业商品的税收存在一些分歧。而且，你知道，现在正是我们需要扩大规模的时候。我们去的时候，已经五天没有任何商品进入了。我们现在看到一些商用卡车在移动。我希望这意味着这个问题已经得到解决，因为我们真正需要的是扩大商业规模并带来更多的新鲜食品和蔬菜。

paras.en: There's a lot of, you know, chocolates and chips coming in and Cokes. That's not really what's needed. And that's because there is bigger margin, I guess, on that and that you don't need a cold chain. But what we need is proper commercial goods coming in, food goods that - you know, the fresh foods, the fresh vegetables and fruits. That's what we need to diversify, but also to bring down the prices on the market so that people with the cash they have can get more.
paras.zh: 你知道，有很多巧克力、薯条和可乐。这并不是真正需要的。我想，那是因为这方面有更大的利润，而且你不需要冷链。但我们需要的是适当的商品进来，食品——你知道，新鲜食品、新鲜蔬菜和水果。这就是我们需要的多元化，同时也需要降低市场价格，以便拥有现金的人们可以获得更多。

paras.en: ROSE: Beyond funding, what else needs to happen to ensure that the necessary aid gets to the people who need it the most?
paras.zh: 罗斯：除了提供资金之外，还需要采取哪些措施来确保最需要的人获得必要的援助？

paras.en: SKAU: Well, I guess, I mean, clearly, there needs to be progress on the peace plan. But, you know, we don't need to wait with early recovery. The big issue there is the dual-use problems. We need UNICEF and other partners to be able to bring in what they need to restore water and sanitation facilities. We need to be able to get the learning material in so we can expand on those temporary learning centers that are there. And there is lots of garbage everywhere. So you can just imagine when the rains start hitting, it's going to be an absolute mess there.
paras.zh: 斯考：嗯，我想，我的意思是，显然，和平计划需要取得进展。但是，你知道，我们不需要等待早日康复。最大的问题是双重用途问题。我们需要联合国儿童基金会和其他合作伙伴提供恢复供水和卫生设施所需的资源。我们需要能够获取学习材料，以便我们可以扩展那里的临时学习中心。而且到处都有很多垃圾。所以你可以想象一下，当雨开始袭来时，那里将会变得一团糟。

paras.en: But on the food side, again, I mean, you know, us now moving into a period where we have to cut 500,000 - half a million people - off our assistance, this is going to cause additional pressure just as the winter hit. And so we need to avoid that. We need donors to step up with funding. But we, of course, also need international community to step up and push forward on the political tracks so there is a solution here. Three years into this, you know, life is at a standstill. They need some hope, and they need to be given the basics to start rebuilding their lives.
paras.zh: 但在食品方面，我的意思是，我们现在正进入一个必须削减 50 万（50 万人）援助的时期，这将在冬季来临之际造成额外的压力。所以我们需要避免这种情况。我们需要捐助者加大资金投入。但当然，我们也需要国际社会在政治轨道上加紧推动，以便找到解决方案。三年过去了，你知道，生活陷入了停滞。他们需要一些希望，需要获得开始重建生活的基础。

paras.en: ROSE: I've been speaking to Carl Skau. He is the acting executive director of the U.N.'s World Food Programme. Thank you very much for joining us.
paras.zh: 罗斯：我一直在和卡尔·斯考谈过。他是联合国世界粮食计划署代理执行主任。非常感谢您加入我们。

articles.title: Political rivals implicated under Pakistan's anti-terror law
articles.author: Betsy Joles

paras.en: Political rivals implicated under Pakistan's anti-terror law
paras.zh: 政治对手受到巴基斯坦反恐法的牵连

paras.en: Pakistan's political showdown continues as more opposition figures are implicated under Pakistan's anti-terror law.
paras.zh: 随着越来越多的反对派人士受到巴基斯坦反恐法的牵连，巴基斯坦的政治摊牌仍在继续。

paras.en: Pakistan's political showdown continues. The former leader of a fractious province that borders Afghanistan has officially been added to a major terrorism case, joining a long list of political figures implicated under anti-terrorism legislation. Betsy Joles has more on this from Islamabad.
paras.zh: 巴基斯坦的政治摊牌仍在继续。与阿富汗接壤的一个脾气暴躁的省份的前领导人已正式被纳入一起重大恐怖主义案件，加入了受反恐立法牵连的一长串政治人物名单。贝特西·乔尔斯 (Betsy Joles) 在伊斯兰堡报道了更多相关内容。

paras.en: BETSY JOLES, BYLINE: Pakistan's Anti-Terrorism Act came into effect in 1997. At that time, sectarian and ethnic violence was raging in two of the country's most populous provinces. The anti-terrorism law provided a parallel legal system for speedier trials of those accused. Then came the U.S.-led war on terror. This is George W. Bush in 2001.
paras.zh: 贝西·乔尔斯连线：巴基斯坦的《反恐法》于 1997 年生效。当时，宗派和种族暴力在该国人口最多的两个省份肆虐。反恐法提供了一个平行的法律制度，以加快对被告的审判。随后美国领导的反恐战争爆发了。这是2001年的乔治·W·布什。

paras.en: GEORGE W BUSH: Our war on terror begins with al-Qaida, but it does not end there. It will not end until every terrorist group of global reach has been found, stopped and defeated.
paras.zh: 乔治·W·布什：我们的反恐战争始于基地组织，但并没有结束。直到每一个影响全球的恐怖组织都被找到、制止和击败为止，这场战争才会结束。

paras.en: JOLES: In the aftermath of 9/11, Pakistan's border belt became a base for militants regrouping after the U.S. invasion of Afghanistan. That gave rise to other insurgencies, like the Tehrik-e Taliban Pakistan, or Pakistan Taliban, in 2007. They'd go on to carry out attack after attack in Pakistan. Here's news of one particularly deadly attack at the Army Public School in Peshawar broadcast on Geo News.
paras.zh: 乔尔斯：9/11 事件发生后，巴基斯坦边境地区成为美国入侵阿富汗后武装分子重新集结的基地。这引发了其他叛乱组织，例如 2007 年的巴基斯坦塔利班运动（Tehrik-e Taliban）或巴基斯坦塔利班（Pakistan Taliban）。他们在巴基斯坦发动了一次又一次的袭击。以下是《地理新闻》播出的白沙瓦陆军公立学校发生的一次特别致命的袭击事件的新闻。

paras.en: UNIDENTIFIED REPORTER: (Non-English language spoken).
paras.zh: 身份不明的记者：（非英语语言）。

paras.en: JOLES: Anti-terrorism courts were one way to try militants. But by this time, anti-terrorism legislation had also been used in cases involving politicians. Nawaz Sharif, the brother of the current prime minister, faced charges under it in 2000, as did General Pervez Musharraf, who overthrew Sharif in a military coup a year earlier. Zoha Waseem, a researcher focused on policing in Pakistan, says it ties back to the law's wording.
paras.zh: 乔尔斯：反恐法庭是审判武装分子的一种方式。但此时，反恐立法也被用于涉及政客的案件。现任总理的兄弟纳瓦兹·谢里夫 (Nawaz Sharif) 于 2000 年面临该罪的指控，一年前在军事政变中推翻谢里夫的佩尔韦兹·穆沙拉夫 (Pervez Musharraf) 将军也面临同样的指控。专注于巴基斯坦治安问题的研究员佐哈·瓦西姆 (Zoha Waseem) 表示，这与法律的措辞有关。

paras.en: ZOHA WASEEM: Terrorism is very broadly defined, and that's been the case for a few decades now under this law.
paras.zh: 佐哈·瓦西姆：恐怖主义的定义非常广泛，根据这项法律，几十年来一直如此。

paras.en: JOLES: In the years since its inception, the law was amended several times to expand its definition and the powers it granted to law enforcement. These days, it could mean...
paras.zh: 乔尔斯：自该法颁布以来，该法已多次修订，以扩大其定义和赋予执法部门的权力。如今，这可能意味着...

paras.en: WASEEM: Anything from kidnapping for ransom, street crime, money laundering or supporting an organization that is considered to be banned.
paras.zh: WASEEM：从绑架勒索、街头犯罪、洗钱或支持被视为禁止的组织等任何行为。

paras.en: JOLES: The terrorism case that names Sohail Afridi, the former chief minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, now under emergency rule, relates to an attack on a state-run radio station. Supporters of former Prime Minister Imran Khan stormed the building and set it on fire after he was arrested in 2023. Footage from elsewhere in Pakistan that day shows Khan's supporters running through the street waving his party's flag as smoke billows around them.
paras.zh: 乔尔斯：目前处于紧急状态的开伯尔-普赫图赫瓦省前首席部长索海尔·阿夫里迪的恐怖主义案件与对一家国营广播电台的袭击有关。前总理伊姆兰·汗 (Imran Khan) 于 2023 年被捕后，他的支持者冲进了这座建筑并将其纵火。当天从巴基斯坦其他地方拍摄的视频显示，汗的支持者在街上挥舞着政党旗帜，周围浓烟滚滚。

paras.en: UNIDENTIFIED PERSON: (Shouting in non-English language).
paras.zh: 身份不明的人：（用非英语语言大喊）。

paras.en: JOLES: Khan himself is now facing terrorism charges, so are the leaders of a banned hard-line Islamist party. In recent years, Kashmiri, Pashtun and Baloch activists have been accused of terrorism too.
paras.zh: 乔尔斯：汗本人现在面临恐怖主义指控，被禁止的强硬伊斯兰政党的领导人也是如此。近年来，克什米尔、普什图和俾路支活动人士也被指控犯有恐怖主义行为。

paras.en: SHIREEN MAZARI: The problem is that you're trivializing the anti-terrorism law.
paras.zh: Shireen Mazari：问题在于你轻视了反恐法。

paras.en: JOLES: Shireen Mazari knows the gravity of this law well because her daughter, Imaan Mazari, and son-in-law, Hadi Ali Chattha, are currently being tried under it. They're lawyers and have been in prison since January - first, in a case related to their social media posts and now for charges that include spreading terror. Mazari is a former politician who has, herself, spent time in jail. But with her daughter's situation, she feels powerless.
paras.zh: 乔尔斯：Shireen Mazari 非常了解这项法律的严重性，因为她的女儿 Imaan Mazari 和女婿 Hadi Ali Chattha 目前正在根据该法律接受审判。他们是律师，自一月份以来一直在监狱中 - 首先是因为与他们的社交媒体帖子有关的案件，现在是因为包括散布恐怖在内的指控。马扎里是一名前政客，她本人也曾入狱。但面对女儿的处境，她却感到无能为力。

paras.en: JOLES: There's nothing you can do. For NPR News, I'm Betsy Joles in Islamabad.
paras.zh: 乔尔斯：你无能为力。我是 NPR 新闻的贝特西·乔尔斯 (Betsy Joles)，来自伊斯兰堡。

paras.en: (SOUNDBITE OF ENLUV AND PAUL GRANT'S "JUNGLE GYM")
paras.zh: （ENLUV 和保罗·格兰特的“丛林健身房”原声片段）
