paras.zh: 因此，Facebook 的文件中都出现了很多文件——我知道当听众听到这个消息时，《社会清算》电影就会上映了——通过这些有发现的法庭案件，Meta 内部的人明确表示，“Instagram 是一种毒品。我们基本上是推动者。”原告辩称，一家公司知道其产品可以做什么、可能会造成危害，但却没有采取任何行动。因此，该公司辩称，社交媒体成瘾并不是官方诊断，这意味着我们不应该将这些法庭案件作为依据。

paras.en: It was interesting how hard it was to find legal experts to analyze these cases on the terms of social media addiction. It’s kind of like the word we use to talk about it, but it’s actually not the main character of these trials. The main [characters] of these trials are, like, the kids who are bringing these personal liability cases and the state’s [attorneys] general that are saying, you know, “You defrauded our consumers,” or, um, “You’ve [misled] our consumers.”
paras.zh: 有趣的是，找到法律专家从社交媒体成瘾的角度来分析这些案件是多么困难。这有点像我们用来谈论它的词，但它实际上不是这些试验的主角。这些审判的主要[人物]是，比如，提起这些个人责任案件的孩子和州[总检察长]，他们说，“你欺骗了我们的消费者”，或者，嗯，“你[误导了]我们的消费者。”

paras.en: Feltman: Well, so getting back to individual action, in this idea of addiction or at least, you know, excessive, unhappy social media use. You talk to folks who are really treating this in themselves as an addiction, including with 12-step programs. Could you tell us a little bit about how this seems to be similar to, you know, treating drug or alcohol addiction and how it seems to be different?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：好吧，那么回到个人行为上来，在成瘾的概念中，或者至少，你知道，过度、不愉快地使用社交媒体。您与那些真正将其视为一种瘾的人进行了交谈，其中包括 12 步计划。您能否告诉我们一些这与治疗毒瘾或酒精成瘾有何相似之处以及有何不同？

paras.en: Parshall: I talked to one woman who I met through this Internet and Technology Addicts Anonymous. And she had her own struggles with alcoholism, and she has been clean and sober for 30 years now, and from alcohol specifically.
paras.zh: 帕歇尔：我通过互联网和技术成瘾者互诫协会认识了一位女士。她自己也曾与酗酒作过斗争，30年来她一直保持干净和清醒，尤其是戒酒。

paras.en: And then, you know, when Facebook came out, she kind of realized that she was getting sucked in. And sometime in the last, I believe it was five years, she managed to start attending these basically AA meetings but for technology and get sober from that. She says that it feels like the same thing to her. Like, internally, this, like, loss of control, this [is] doing things that she doesn’t want to do and looking around at the people in her life that she feels like she’s constantly letting down and are increasingly learning to expect very little of her as, like, kind of the same kind of heartbreak.
paras.zh: 然后，你知道，当 Facebook 出现时，她有点意识到自己被吸引了。在过去的某个时候，我相信是五年了，她设法开始参加这些基本上 AA 的会议，但为了技术，并从中清醒过来。她说这对她来说感觉是一样的。就像，在内心，这，就像，失去控制，这是做她不想做的事情，环顾她生活中的人，她觉得自己一直在失望，并且越来越学会对她抱有很少的期望，就像，类似的心碎。

paras.en: It seems from talking to these people who go to these 12-step programs that, for certain people, they can be really beneficial in the same way that they’re really beneficial for people who are struggling with other addictions. I mean, just from the outside looking in, it seems like a lot of that is down to community support and dedication. You get involved in these programs, and you can just go to meetings. There’s, like, a saying, “Meeting makers make it.” But also a lot of the people I talked to said, like, getting involved, volunteering, helping run the meetings, everything like that really helped pull them out.
paras.zh: 从与参加这些 12 步计划的人交谈看来，对于某些人来说，这些计划确实有益，就像它们对那些与其他成瘾作斗争的人确实有益一样。我的意思是，仅从外部来看，这似乎很大程度上归功于社区的支持和奉献。您可以参与这些计划，并且可以直接参加会议。有句话说：“会议制造者成功”。但也有很多与我交谈过的人说，参与、志愿服务、帮助主持会议，诸如此类的一切确实帮助他们摆脱了困境。

paras.en: And I think some of that is, like, it’s something to fill your life with purpose, becoming a sponsor for other people. You know, some of the addiction researchers I talked to pointed out that there’s a reason that you’re smoking all the time, or there’s a reason that you are filling all your time with TikTok. I mean, I feel that way, like, at times of life when I feel that TikTok is hardest to resist is when everything else feels like a monumental effort, and scrolling is the only thing that can, kind of, turn my brain off. The things that 12-step programs and then other forms of treatment that are more clinically evidence-based, like, you know, seeing psychologists or therapists, many of which do use 12 steps but—can help you, kind of, fill that gap or fill that hole or however you wanna think about what it is that the vice is coming into your life to replace or to fill.
paras.zh: 我认为其中一些是，比如，它可以让你的生活充满目标，成为其他人的赞助者。你知道，我采访过的一些成瘾研究人员指出，你一直抽烟是有原因的，或者你一直用 TikTok 打发时间也是有原因的。我的意思是，我有这种感觉，就像在生活中，当我觉得 TikTok 是最难以抗拒的时候，其他一切都感觉像是一项巨大的努力，而滚动是唯一可以让我的大脑停止运转的东西。 12步计划以及更多基于临床证据的其他形式的治疗，比如，你知道，去看心理学家或治疗师，其中许多确实使用了12步，但可以帮助你，某种程度上，填补这个空白或填补那个漏洞，或者无论你想思考恶习正在进入你的生活来取代或填补什么。

paras.en: And so, yeah, I think that could be done through 12-step programs. For some people, those don’t work very well ’cause they have such a heavy focus on sobriety. You can get trapped in a cycle of shame of, like, getting sober and then breaking it and then hating yourself and coming back crawling, and for some people, that just doesn’t work well. Addiction treatment in general is kind of trying to move away from the sobriety approach to a more evidence-based harm reduction. Like, okay, we’re not going to say you have to be 100 percent sober from this thing. You see this with sex and porn addiction a lot where, like, that can be a really harmful cycle.
paras.zh: 所以，是的，我认为这可以通过 12 步计划来完成。对于某些人来说，这些方法效果不太好，因为他们非常注重清醒。你可能会陷入羞耻的循环中，比如，清醒了，然后打破它，然后讨厌自己，然后爬回来，对某些人来说，这不太有效。一般来说，成瘾治疗是一种试图从清醒的方法转向更加基于证据的减少伤害的方法。就像，好吧，我们不会说你必须在这件事上百分百清醒。你在性和色情成瘾中经常看到这种情况，这可能是一个非常有害的循环。

paras.en: And so the point of therapy might not necessarily be: we’re gonna cut out social media entirely. It might be: we’re going to build these guardrails around it, or we’re gonna make sure that you find a way to only stick to just a little bit. For some people, that’s also not possible, and that’s why they go for the whole sobriety thing. The researchers and clinicians and people who have been through these 12-step programs, they all kind of stress that, like, you need to have compassion with yourself and find something that works for you.
paras.zh: 因此，治疗的重点可能不一定是：我们要完全切断社交媒体。可能是：我们将围绕它建立这些护栏，或者我们将确保你找到一种只坚持一点点的方法。对于某些人来说，这也是不可能的，这就是为什么他们追求整个清醒的事情。研究人员、临床医生以及经历过这些 12 步计划的人都强调，你需要对自己有同情心，并找到适合你的东西。

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah, I know that, for me personally, relative to how much I was on social media until this point, for the last couple of years, I’ve been, like, functionally not on social media. And it’s really interesting because, every once in a while, I start to feel, you know, disconnected enough that I really want to, like, be spending some time on Instagram on my phone, and I redownload it. And the first couple times this happened, it was a real shame cycle because I was like, “Wow, I can’t do it in moderation.”
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的，我知道，就我个人而言，相对于我在社交媒体上的使用程度而言，在过去的几年里，我一直在功能上不使用社交媒体。这真的很有趣，因为每隔一段时间，我就会开始感到，你知道，我真的很想在手机上花一些时间在 Instagram 上，然后我重新下载它。前几次这种情况发生时，这是一个真正的耻辱循环，因为我想，“哇，我不能适度地做到这一点。”

paras.en: And now I’ve really, I think, successfully reframed it as less of trying to be sober from social media and more like detoxing, where it’s like, you know, I know what it feels like when it doesn’t feel good anymore. And, like, when I really miss it in a way that feels kind of holistic and healthy and that, like, I just sort of want to be enjoying the Internet again, I redownload it. And then when I get to the point where I’m like, “Oh, no, now, now it’s poisoned my brain again,” then I get rid of it for a while.
paras.zh: 我想，现在我真的已经成功地将其重新定义为不再试图从社交媒体中保持清醒，而更像是排毒，就像，你知道，我知道当感觉不再舒服时是什么感觉。当我真的以一种整体和健康的方式想念它时，就像我只是想再次享受互联网一样，我会重新下载它。然后当我想到“哦，不，现在，它又毒害了我的大脑”时，我就会暂时摆脱它。

paras.en: And I think it does, for me at least, seem to work in terms of, like, recalibrating me to stop, the decreased sensitivity to it where you’re just, like, totally desensitized and spending more and more time on there and not actually using it for the things that, like, again, are prosocial and actually feel good, like reaching out to friends and seeing cool art they’re making and stuff. But, yeah, I feel like it—what that looks like is [so] personal and context dependent that it feels really tough and unfair that, like, everybody has to figure out what that looks like for them.
paras.zh: 我认为，至少对我来说，它似乎确实有效，比如，重新调整我停下来，对它的敏感度降低，你只是，就像，完全麻木不仁，花越来越多的时间在那里，而不是真正将它用于那些亲社会的、实际上感觉良好的事情上，比如与朋友接触，看看他们正在制作的很酷的艺术之类的东西。但是，是的，我觉得它看起来像[如此]个人和环境依赖，感觉真的很难和不公平，就像，每个人都必须弄清楚对他们来说是什么样子。

paras.en: Parshall: And it’s constantly changing, too. That’s the thing that gets me. Like, I feel like I’ve navigated, I’ve, like, negotiated a good relationship, and then it changes. It’s kind of like the slippery slope doesn’t stop.
paras.zh: Parshall：而且它也在不断变化。这就是让我着迷的事情。就像，我觉得我已经找到了方向，我已经谈判了一段良好的关系，然后它就发生了变化。这有点像滑坡不会停止。

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah, the algorithm changes; what’s going on in your life changes.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的，算法改变了；你生活中发生的事情会改变。

paras.en: Parshall: I think part of that is, like, the way they’re designed to, like, kind of keep it as a slow slope. So, like, even if you start it with a good relationship, it is pretty easy to stop, and then you look up and you go, “Where am I?” And then you delete the app because you’re like, “I don’t like that I’m here.” I think your point about reframing is a really good one and one that I wanna stress that, like, if the addiction framing to you feels like it is unhelpful, it is really not necessary that you think of it as addiction.
paras.zh: 帕歇尔：我认为其中一部分原因是它们的设计方式，比如保持缓慢的斜坡。所以，即使你以良好的关系开始，也很容易停下来，然后你抬头看去，“我在哪里？”然后你删除了该应用程序，因为你会想，“我不喜欢我在这里。”我认为你关于重构的观点非常好，我想强调的是，如果你觉得成瘾框架没有帮助，那么你真的没有必要将其视为成瘾。

paras.en: There’s a lot of other ways to think about it. Some researchers really like just thinking about it as a habit. And the differences between those things are a little bit hard to literally pin down. You know, a habit is like biting your nails. We don’t really say people are addicted to biting their nails, but it’s like there’s a particular cue: “I’m bored; I’m anxious.” With your phone it might be “It’s bedtime,” and you develop these habits.
paras.zh: 还有很多其他的方式来思考它。一些研究人员真的喜欢将其视为一种习惯。这些事物之间的差异有点难以从字面上确定。你知道，习惯就像咬指甲一样。我们并不是说人们沉迷于咬指甲，但这就像有一个特定的暗示：“我很无聊；我很焦虑。”当你使用手机时，“该睡觉了”，你就养成了这些习惯。

paras.en: And, like, you know the thing where, like, you literally can open Instagram through muscle memory or any other app that you use and start scrolling and realize you didn’t even realize that you’d chosen to do it? So, like, the researchers I talk to stress that, like, we do know how to get people to change their habits. I mean, we have more research than we do maybe on, like, tech addiction. You can shuffle around the way the apps are on the home screen. You can delete them entirely. Something I do with TikTok is: on the iPhone, it lets you remove it from your home screen but not from your phone entirely, so every time I want it, I have to search for TikTok. That doesn’t always work. Um, but it stops, it stops me from having a literal rote muscle memory on it. I might need to do that with Instagram soon, honestly. So yeah, there’s little tweaks that you can do to try to resist this thing that is probably, profit-motive-wise, going to continue to exist to want to pull you in.
paras.zh: 而且，就像，你知道这样的事情，比如，你真的可以通过肌肉记忆或你使用的任何其他应用程序打开 Instagram，然后开始滚动，然后意识到你甚至没有意识到你选择这样做？因此，与我交谈的研究人员强调，我们确实知道如何让人们改变习惯。我的意思是，我们对科技成瘾的研究可能比我们所做的还要多。您可以随意切换应用程序在主屏幕上的显示方式。您可以完全删除它们。我对 TikTok 所做的事情是：在 iPhone 上，它可以让你将其从主屏幕上删除，但不能完全从手机上删除，所以每次我想要它时，我都必须搜索 TikTok。但这并不总是有效。嗯，但是它停止了，它阻止了我对它进行死记硬背的肌肉记忆。老实说，我可能很快就需要在 Instagram 上做到这一点。所以，是的，你可以做一些小小的调整来尝试抵制这种事情，从利润动机的角度来看，这种事情可能会继续存在，想要把你拉进来。

paras.en: And you don’t have to think of it like addiction if you don’t want to. That can be a really stigmatizing framework, and it can be one that, you know, I mean, especially with alcoholism, like, the, kind of, the way that people who are alcoholics talk about it often is like, “I am an alcoholic,” and for the rest of your life, you frame yourself as an alcoholic. You’re just, like, in recovery. People I talk to in 12-step programs, some of them did have that framing for tech addiction. But I would say their experience is, like, more extreme than a lot of the people that I know who use technology—in, subjectively, in their experience—too much.
paras.zh: 如果您不愿意，您不必将其视为上瘾。这可能是一个非常侮辱性的框架，我的意思是，特别是对于酗酒，就像酗酒者经常谈论的方式一样，“我是一个酒鬼”，在你的余生中，你把自己定位为一个酒鬼。你只是在康复中。我在 12 步计划中交谈过的人中，有些人确实有这样的技术成瘾框架。但我想说，他们的经历比我认识的许多过度使用技术的人（主观上，在他们的经历中）更加极端。

paras.en: Feltman: We’ve brushed against this, but I would love to hear where you actually have landed in terms of managing your own screen use and social media use?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：我们反对这一点，但我很想听听您在管理自己的屏幕使用和社交媒体使用方面实际上取得了哪些进展？

paras.en: Parshall: Yeah, I would love to say that I cut down my screen time drastically. When I first started this story, I was like, “How great of an arc would it be if, at the end, I can say that I managed to cut it down to three hours a day, and here’s what I did?” I did not do that. My screen time last week was higher than ever, but I was sick, in my defense.
paras.zh: 帕歇尔：是的，我想说我大大减少了看屏幕的时间。当我第一次开始写这个故事时，我想，“如果最后我可以说我设法把它减少到每天三个小时，而这就是我所做的，那该有多棒啊？”我没有那样做。上周我看电视的时间比以往任何时候都多，但我为自己辩护，我病了。

paras.en: And I think what I’ve noticed through observing these Sunday screen time notifications every week is: it really depends on the type of week I had. And there isn’t some terrible trend line for me where it’s getting worse and worse and worse and worse. It looks like this more than anything. And I think taking the advice of the researchers I talked to who said to give yourself grace ’cause you’re in kind of a screwed-up system, I’ve been trying to do that.
paras.zh: 我认为通过每周观察这些周日屏幕时间通知，我注意到的是：这实际上取决于我一周的类型。对我来说，不存在任何可怕的趋势线，情况会变得越来越糟。看起来比什么都重要。我认为，根据与我交谈过的研究人员的建议，他们说要给自己宽容，因为你正处于一个搞砸的系统中，我一直在努力这样做。

paras.en: I’ve also been trying to listen to myself when I have that little voice in my head that’s saying, like, “You’re doing this to numb yourself,” and the things that are worth living about life in the physical world are things that take time to build. Like, you’re gonna have to go through going to, like, a deeply unpleasant social situation for a little while in order to meet the friends, to meet the friends, to meet the friends, instead of just focusing on the vicious cycle of screen time, thinking of the virtuous cycle of doing things that you’re passionate about and that can be on a screen. Trying to not have this bifurcation in my head of, like, screen time—bad. Like, noticing when I have had seven hours of screen time, being like, “Oh, actually four of those was ’cause I was reading a book I really liked, and that’s okay.” So yeah, I, I haven’t fixed myself. But I do think I’ve started to pay more attention in a way that is healthier. I would say I hope other people can, too, but I know that I’m not leading the charge on this. I’m in the muck with every single person in my life, trying to figure out what works for them. So I hope you’re able to, to make it work better for you, too.
paras.zh: 当我脑海中出现一个小声音时，我也一直在尝试倾听自己的声音，比如“你这样做是为了麻痹自己”，而物质世界中值得生活的事情是需要时间来建立的。就像，你将不得不经历一段时间的非常不愉快的社交场合，以便与朋友见面，与朋友见面，与朋友见面，而不是仅仅关注屏幕时间的恶性循环，思考做你热爱的事情并且可以在屏幕上进行的良性循环。试图不让我的头脑中出现这样的分歧，比如屏幕时间，这很糟糕。就像，注意到当我有七个小时的屏幕时间时，我会说，“哦，实际上其中四个小时是因为我正在读一本我真正喜欢的书，那没关系。”所以是的，我，我还没有修复自己。但我确实认为我已经开始以更健康的方式更加关注。我想说我希望其他人也能这样做，但我知道我并不是这方面的带头人。我和生活中的每一个人都陷入困境，试图找出对他们有用的方法。所以我希望你也能够让它更好地为你工作。

paras.en: Feltman: Thank you so much for that. And, thank you for coming on to talk about your story with us.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：非常感谢你。并且，感谢您抽空与我们谈论您的故事。

paras.en: Feltman: That’s all for today’s episode. You can check out Allison’s feature article online or in the latest issue of Scientific American, on newsstands now. We’ll be back on Monday with our weekly science news roundup.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：这就是今天这一集的全部内容。您可以在线查看艾莉森的专题文章，也可以在报摊上最新一期的《科学美国人》中查看。我们将于周一带着每周科学新闻综述回来。

paras.en: For Scientific American, this is Rachel Feltman. Have a great weekend!
paras.zh: 《科学美国人》的这位人物是雷切尔·费尔特曼 (Rachel Feltman)。周末愉快！

articles.title: How many planets could fit in the solar system?

paras.en: When I was a kid, I once watched a science-fiction flick called Journey to the Far Side of the Sun. The story’s main conceit was that scientists discover an Earth-like planet directly opposite our own in the same orbit around the sun, always hidden from our vantage point. The plot itself was somewhat silly, but the idea of a counter-Earth really stuck with me.
paras.zh: 当我还是个孩子的时候，我曾经看过一部科幻电影，名叫《太阳背面之旅》。这个故事的主要构想是，科学家们发现了一颗类地行星，与我们的行星直接相对，在同一轨道上围绕太阳运行，但总是隐藏在我们的有利位置之外。情节本身有点愚蠢，但反地球的想法确实让我着迷。

paras.en: We know no such planet exists in real life, though; its gravitational effects on other worlds such as Mars and Venus would be obvious. Also, we’ve sent probes all through the solar system, and they’ve never spotted such a planetary arrangement.
paras.zh: 不过，我们知道现实生活中并不存在这样的行星。它对火星和金星等其他世界的引力影响是显而易见的。此外，我们已经向整个太阳系发送了探测器，但他们从未发现过这样的行星排列。

paras.en: But is this possible? Could two planets physically share the same orbit? The circumstances would have to be just right, and such a situation would be incredibly unlikely to occur. But the answer, surprisingly, is yes. In fact, many planets can technically share the same orbit! And when they do, their behavior gets pretty weird.
paras.zh: 但这可能吗？两颗行星实际上可以共享相同的轨道吗？情况必须恰到好处，而这种情况极不可能发生。但令人惊讶的是，答案是肯定的。事实上，从技术上讲，许多行星可以共享相同的轨道！当他们这样做时，他们的行为就会变得非常奇怪。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The basic physics of how one object orbits another—say, a planet revolving around a star—has been known since Isaac Newton’s day. The math for such a simple system is pretty straightforward. And it’s deterministic; once you write down the equations, you can predict what the system will look like as far into the future or past as you like.
paras.zh: 自艾萨克·牛顿时代以来，一个物体如何绕另一个物体（例如行星绕恒星旋转）运行的基本物理原理就为人所知。这样一个简单系统的数学计算非常简单。而且它是确定性的；一旦写下方程式，您就可以根据需要预测系统在未来或过去的样子。

paras.en: Throw in a third massive object, though, and the math gets ridiculously more complicated and difficult to solve. Under some circumstances, however, solutions exist that allow for a stable system even if two such planets interact. One of those solutions is a bit of weirdness called a horseshoe orbit, and it relies on a quirk of orbital mechanics.
paras.zh: 然而，如果再加上第三个巨大的物体，数学就会变得更加复杂和难以解决。然而，在某些情况下，即使两个这样的行星相互作用，也存在允许系统稳定的解决方案。其中一个解决方案有点奇怪，称为马蹄轨道，它依赖于轨道力学的一个怪癖。

paras.en: Imagine that two planets orbit a star on very similar paths, but one (call it Planet 1) is just barely closer to the star than the other (Planet 2). This inner planet, being closer, will move more rapidly around the star than the outer planet. Eventually it will catch up to Planet 2. What happens next is counterintuitive: instead of smashing into each other, or one of them getting flung away on a high-speed slingshot trajectory, they will start to interact gravitationally while they are still hundreds of thousands of kilometers apart. Looking just at Planet 1 for a moment, it will be pulled ahead by Planet 2’s gravity, giving it more orbital energy.
paras.zh: 想象一下，两颗行星以非常相似的路径围绕一颗恒星运行，但一颗行星（称为行星 1）仅比另一颗行星（行星 2）更靠近恒星。这颗内行星距离较近，将比外行星更快地绕恒星运行。最终它将赶上第二颗行星。接下来发生的事情是违反直觉的：它们不会相互撞击，或者其中一个在高速弹弓轨迹上被甩开，而是在彼此相距数十万公里的情况下开始进行引力相互作用。看看行星 1，它会被行星 2 的引力拉向前方，从而赋予它更多的轨道能量。

paras.en: This is where the oddity of orbital mechanics really factors in: if you give an object more energy (say, by accelerating it), it will naturally move to a higher orbit, one with a larger radius. So as Planet 1 accelerates, it moves slightly outward from the star. But objects in larger orbits move slower. Thus, Planet 1 slows down and begins to lag behind Planet 2, widening the gap between them. As seen from Planet 2, Planet 1 will appear to approach on the inside lane, slow down, move to the outside lane and then fall away once again. It’s as if Planet 2 has repelled its sister world! In reality, both objects orbit the star in the same direction, just at different, changing speeds.
paras.zh: 这就是轨道力学的奇怪之处真正起作用的地方：如果你给一个物体更多的能量（比如，通过加速它），它自然会移动到一个更高的轨道，一个半径更大的轨道。因此，当行星 1 加速时，它会稍微向外移动。但轨道较大的物体运动速度较慢。因此，行星 1 减速并开始落后于行星 2，从而扩大了它们之间的差距。从行星 2 中可以看出，行星 1 似乎会从内侧车道接近，减速，移动到外侧车道，然后再次脱离。就好像第二颗行星已经排斥了它的姐妹世界一样！事实上，这两个物体都以相同的方向绕恒星运行，只是以不同的速度变化。

paras.en: But what about Planet 2? It’s affected by Planet 1’s gravity during the encounter as well. Planet 1 pulls Planet 2 backward, stealing some of the latter’s orbital energy. That drops Planet 2 into a smaller orbit, where it speeds up and moves ahead of Planet 1. So now Planet 1 is on the outside path, and Planet 2 on the inside. They’ve swapped orbits!
paras.zh: 但是行星 2 呢？在遭遇过程中它也会受到 1 号行星引力的影响。行星 1 将行星 2 向后拉，窃取了后者的一些轨道能量。这使得行星 2 进入一个较小的轨道，在那里它加速并移动到行星 1 的前面。所以现在行星 1 位于外侧路径，行星 2 位于内侧。他们交换了轨道！

paras.en: Eventually they meet again, and this time the roles are reversed: they swap orbits once more, and we’re back to the original situation.
paras.zh: 最终他们再次相遇，这次角色互换：他们再次交换轨道，我们又回到了原来的情况。

paras.en: This is not just theoretical; we see this happening in the solar system. Saturn has a pair of moons called Janus and Epimetheus, which orbit the planet on paths that are only 50 kilometers different in radius, and they undergo exactly this orbit swapping every four years or so. So not only does this occur in real life, but it’s actually a stable configuration.
paras.zh: 这不仅仅是理论上的；而且是现实的。我们在太阳系中看到了这种情况的发生。土星有一对卫星，分别称为 Janus 和 Epimetheus，它们绕土星运行的路径半径仅相差 50 公里，并且它们每四年左右就会进行一次轨道交换。所以这不仅发生在现实生活中，而且实际上是一个稳定的配置。

paras.en: That means two planets can indeed share (or nearly share) the same orbit. And while they will encounter each other, they can do so safely.
paras.zh: 这意味着两个行星确实可以共享（或几乎共享）相同的轨道。虽然他们会相遇，但他们可以安全地进行。

paras.en: But what about an arrangement with more co-orbital planets, such as, say, three? Does that work?
paras.zh: 但是如果有更多的共轨行星（例如三颗）呢？那有用吗？

paras.en: According to research by a team of international scientists published in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (MNRAS), yes, you can have more than two planets share an orbit. Astonishingly, many more can coexist!
paras.zh: 根据英国皇家天文学会月刊 (MNRAS) 上发表的国际科学家团队的研究，是的，可以有两个以上的行星共享一个轨道。令人惊讶的是，更多的东西可以共存！

paras.en: First, the researchers used the mathematics of orbital mechanics to simulate the physics of two Earth-sized planets orbiting a sunlike star at 150 million kilometers (the real life Earth-sun distance) and showed they can persist in such horseshoe orbits for billions of years! Then the team added more and more planets to see what would happen.
paras.zh: 首先，研究人员利用轨道力学数学模拟了两颗地球大小的行星围绕一颗距离 1.5 亿公里（现实生活中的地日距离）的类日恒星运行的物理现象，并表明它们可以在这样的马蹄形轨道上持续数十亿年！然后团队添加了越来越多的行星来看看会发生什么。

paras.en: When two planets meet up with each other, they swap orbits, as is already understood. But eventually one will then approach the third planet. When it does, they swap orbits and move apart. Eventually one of those two meets up with the first planet, and the whole situation repeats. This happens with every planet-on-planet encounter.
paras.zh: 正如人们已经了解的那样，当两颗行星相遇时，它们会交换轨道。但最终一颗行星将接近第三颗行星。当它发生时，它们交换轨道并分开。最终，这两颗行星中的一颗与第一颗行星相遇，整个情况又重复了。每次行星间的相遇都会发生这种情况。

paras.en: Incredibly, the scientists found this to be true if they had as many as 24 Earth-sized planets packed into a single orbit! Twenty-four! That shocked me. Still, it seems to work in the simulations; any planet can’t get very far along its path without meeting another, and when the two do so, they swap positions and continue on until the next encounter with the next planet down the line, constantly sliding around and jockeying for position.
paras.zh: 令人难以置信的是，科学家们发现，如果他们有多达 24 颗地球大小的行星挤在一个轨道上，这就是真的！ 24！这让我很震惊。尽管如此，它在模拟中似乎还是有效的。任何一颗行星都不可能在不遇到另一个行星的情况下沿着它的路径走得很远，当两个行星这样做时，它们会交换位置并继续前进，直到下一次遇到下一个行星，不断地滑动并争夺位置。

paras.en: The scientists even tried this in a simulation of our own solar system, which, they found, could support the addition of an extra couple of Earths or Venuses—or another Mercury or Mars.
paras.zh: 科学家们甚至在我们自己的太阳系的模拟中尝试过这一点，他们发现，这可以支持添加额外的几个地球或金星，或者另一个水星或火星。

paras.en: Creating a system like this isn’t easy. It’s possible that a very thick ring of dust around a star could form several planets in the same orbit simultaneously, though conditions would have to be rather fine-tuned to allow that to happen. Also, planets can migrate toward and away from their host star on much grander scales as they interact gravitationally. And if enough smaller planets get tossed around by this process, they could also end up in shared orbits.
paras.zh: 创建这样的系统并不容易。恒星周围非常厚的尘埃环有可能同时在同一轨道上形成多颗行星，尽管必须对条件进行相当微调才能实现这种情况。此外，当行星通过引力相互作用时，它们可以在更大的范围内向主恒星迁移或远离主恒星。如果有足够多的较小行星在这个过程中被抛来抛去，它们也可能最终进入共享轨道。

paras.en: Detecting such planetary systems from Earth is possible, too. One way we find planets now is through the transit method, in which a planet passing directly in front of its star creates a mini eclipse, as seen from Earth. If several transits occur in sequence when we should only see one for that particular orbit, that would be a sign. Also, the fact that planets in this arrangement slide along their orbit and swap positions means that their positions in that orbit change, which, in turn, changes the timing of the transits. That would be detectable, too, even if all of the planets don’t actually join the transit parade.
paras.zh: 从地球上探测此类行星系统也是可能的。我们现在寻找行星的一种方法是通过凌日法，即一颗行星直接从其恒星前面经过，会产生一次小型日食，就像从地球上看到的那样。如果在该特定轨道上我们只能看到一次凌日时，连续发生了几次凌日，这将是一个迹象。此外，这种排列中的行星沿着其轨道滑动并交换位置的事实意味着它们在该轨道中的位置发生变化，这反过来又改变了凌日的时间。即使并非所有行星都真正加入过境游行，这也是可以检测到的。

paras.en: Delightfully, the authors of the MNRAS study speculate that there is another way to form these systems: building them on purpose. Having multiple worlds all in one orbit might be handy for interplanetary travel. And while moving them around physically is a daunting task, a sufficiently technologically advanced alien civilization might feel that it’s worth the effort. If we ever were to find such a system, well, that would be interesting, wouldn’t it?
paras.zh: 令人高兴的是，MNRAS 研究的作者推测还有另一种方法可以形成这些系统：有目的地构建它们。在一个轨道上拥有多个世界对于星际旅行可能会很方便。虽然移动它们是一项艰巨的任务，但技术足够先进的外星文明可能会觉得这是值得的。如果我们找到这样一个系统，那会很有趣，不是吗？

paras.en: What a way to discover aliens exist! And it would really make me reassess my opinion on Journey to the Far Side of the Sun—possibly
paras.zh: 这是发现外星人存在的好方法！这真的会让我重新评估我对《太阳的背面之旅》的看法——可能

articles.title: 5 ways to make Halloween decorations friendlier to wildlife

paras.en: Recently, a slender, yellow-striped California whipsnake, small enough to fit in a person’s hand, was brought to the California Wildlife Center in Calabasas. Its lower body was so twisted in fine strands of fake spiderwebs that it was essentially a ball, with twigs and leaves stuck in the mess.
paras.zh: 最近，一条细长的、黄色条纹的加州鞭蛇，小到足以容纳一个人的手，被带到卡拉巴萨斯的加州野生动物中心。它的下半身被细密的假蜘蛛网扭曲得几乎是一个球，树枝和树叶粘在乱七八糟的东西里。

paras.en: “Had that gone on much longer, it could have started severing into its skin,” says Lauren Michaels, director of animal care at the center. Fortunately, the snake recovered and was eventually released. Not every animal is so lucky, though. Cambria Wells, the center’s education and outreach manager, recalls a hummingbird that was similarly wrapped in webbing and didn’t make it.
paras.zh: 该中心动物护理主任劳伦·迈克尔斯说：“如果这种情况持续更长时间，它可能会开始割伤它的皮肤。”幸运的是，蛇最终康复并被释放。不过，并不是所有动物都这么幸运。该中心的教育和外展经理坎布里亚·威尔斯(Cambria Wells)回忆说，有一只蜂鸟同样被织带包裹着，但没有成功。

paras.en: Every Halloween season, wildlife rehabilitation centers across the country see cases in which birds, bats, snakes, rodents, deer and other wild animals become injured or entangled in seasonal decorations.
paras.zh: 每到万圣节季节，全国各地的野生动物康复中心都会看到鸟类、蝙蝠、蛇、啮齿动物、鹿和其他野生动物受伤或被季节性装饰品缠住的案例。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The good news is that you can have a spooky spectacle in front of your house and still protect wildlife. Here are five ways to make your Halloween display friendlier to the creatures that fly, slither and scurry through your yard.
paras.zh: 好消息是，您可以在自家门前欣赏恐怖奇观，同时仍然可以保护野生动物。这里有五种方法可以让你的万圣节展示对那些在你院子里飞翔、滑行和匆忙的生物更加友好。

paras.en: Of all the Halloween decorations people display outdoors, synthetic spiderwebs are the most dangerous, according to many wildlife experts. Made of strong, stretchy plastic, the webbing’s thin, hard-to-see strands can cling to animals and become wrapped around their bodies, posing a serious entanglement hazard. Trapped animals can go hungry, suffer constriction injuries, or even dislocate their limbs as they struggle to free themselves, Wells explains.
paras.zh: 许多野生动物专家表示，在人们户外展示的所有万圣节装饰品中，合成蜘蛛网是最危险的。这种带子由坚固、有弹性的塑料制成，细而难以看见的线会粘在动物身上并缠绕在它们的身体上，造成严重的缠绕危险。威尔斯解释说，被困的动物可能会挨饿、遭受压迫性伤害，甚至在挣扎着挣脱时四肢脱臼。

paras.en: To get the spiderweb look without the stretchy strands, the best option is a solid web decoration made from rigid plastic or metal, she advises. Rope-style webs are safer than stretchy spiderwebbing, but they can still pose an entanglement risk.
paras.zh: 她建议，为了获得没有弹性线的蜘蛛网外观，最好的选择是由硬质塑料或金属制成的坚固的网状装饰。绳索式网比弹性蜘蛛网更安全，但它们仍然可能造成缠绕风险。

paras.en: If you do use stretchy or rope webbing outdoors, Wells recommends pulling it taut against a solid surface, such as your house, rather than across an open space where an animal could fly or travel through it.
paras.zh: 如果您确实在户外使用弹性织带或绳带，威尔斯建议将其拉紧在坚固的表面（例如您的房子）上，而不是穿过动物可以飞翔或穿过的开放空间。

paras.en: The same principle applies to other decorations. Choose solid objects over anything with netting, strings, ropes, ribbons or other materials in which an animal could become entangled. Think tombstones, solid skeletons, signs or other decorations that hold their shape and don’t have loose or dangling parts.
paras.zh: 同样的原则也适用于其他装饰。选择坚固的物体，而不是任何带有网、绳子、绳子、丝带或其他可能缠住动物的材料的物体。想想墓碑、坚固的骨架、标志或其他保持形状且没有松动或悬垂部件的装饰品。

paras.en: Popular inflatables can be a safer alternative to netting or webbing, but you should make sure their anchoring cords and power cords are secured and check regularly for damage.
paras.zh: 流行的充气玩具可能是比网或织带更安全的替代品，但您应该确保其锚定线和电源线固定并定期检查是否有损坏。

paras.en: In general, look for durable decorations you can reuse year after year rather than items that are designed to be thrown away after a single season to reduce the broader environmental impact of your Halloween display, Wells notes.
paras.zh: 威尔斯指出，一般来说，寻找可以年复一年重复使用的耐用装饰品，而不是设计为在一个季节后丢弃的物品，以减少万圣节展示对环境的更广泛影响。

paras.en: Turn Halloween lights off when you go to bed
paras.zh: 睡觉时关掉万圣节灯

paras.en: “Lighting is an underappreciated form of impact on wildlife,” Wells says. Artificial light can interfere with wildlife behavior and disorient migrating birds, many of which travel during the middle of the night and the early morning at this time of year, she explains.
paras.zh: “照明对野生动物的影响是一种未被充分认识的形式，”威尔斯说。她解释说，人造光会干扰野生动物的行为，并使候鸟迷失方向，其中许多候鸟在每年这个时候的半夜和清晨迁徙。

paras.en: If you want lights as part of your decor, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service recommends opting for ones with warmer colors, such as amber, orange or red, rather than blue, white or other cooler-colored lights, whose shorter wavelengths are more disruptive to biological rhythms.
paras.zh: 如果您希望灯光作为装饰的一部分，美国鱼类和野生动物管理局建议选择暖色灯光，例如琥珀色、橙色或红色，而不是蓝色、白色或其他冷色灯光，这些灯光的波长较短，对生物节律的干扰更大。

paras.en: But regardless of the type of lights you use, the simplest and most effective step, Wells says, is to turn them off when you go to bed, giving wildlife darkness during the overnight hours.
paras.zh: 但韦尔斯说，无论你使用哪种类型的灯，最简单、最有效的步骤就是在睡觉时将其关闭，让野生动物在夜间保持黑暗。

paras.en: Window decals, creepy figures, glowing jack-o’-lanterns and other decorations displayed on or just inside your windows can still be seen from the street without introducing loose materials into your yard that wildlife could encounter.
paras.zh: 窗户贴花、令人毛骨悚然的人物、发光的南瓜灯以及窗户上或窗户内展示的其他装饰品仍然可以从街道上看到，而无需将野生动物可能遇到的松散材料引入您的院子。

paras.en: Pumpkins are a Halloween staple, but you should remember that they’re also food. If you want to keep wildlife from chowing down on your carefully carved jack-o’-lantern without harming any creatures, Wells says, try bringing it in in the evening or coating it with a bitter apple spray or cayenne pepper diluted with water.
paras.zh: 南瓜是万圣节的主食，但你应该记住它们也是食物。威尔斯说，如果你想让野生动物不吃你精心雕刻的南瓜灯，而又不伤害任何生物，可以尝试在晚上把它带进来，或者在上面涂上苦苹果喷雾或用水稀释的辣椒。

paras.en: When spooky season is over, you can then compost your pumpkins or dispose of them according to your local food- or yard-waste guidelines. You can also check whether a local wildlife center or animal sanctuary accepts intact, untreated pumpkins for animal feed.
paras.zh: 当阴森的季节结束后，您可以根据当地的食物或庭院垃圾指南对南瓜进行堆肥或处理。您还可以检查当地野生动物中心或动物保护区是否接受完整的、未经处理的南瓜作为动物饲料。

paras.en: Other natural materials, such as gourds, hay, and cornstalks make for festive decor, but Wells suggests choosing materials from your local area to reduce the risk of introducing invasive plants or seeds.
paras.zh: 其他天然材料，如葫芦、干草和玉米杆，可用于节日装饰，但威尔斯建议选择当地的材料，以减少引入入侵植物或种子的风险。

paras.en: If you find an entangled animal, call for help
paras.zh: 如果发现被缠住的动物，请寻求帮助

paras.en: If you discover an animal caught in or injured by Halloween decorations, resist the urge to untangle and release it. Injuries may not be obvious at first, and the animal may need medical care.
paras.zh: 如果您发现动物被万圣节装饰品卡住或受伤，请克制住解开并释放它的冲动。受伤一开始可能并不明显，动物可能需要医疗护理。

paras.en: Instead contact a local wildlife rehabilitation center for guidance. You can find nearby resources through Animal Help Now.
paras.zh: 相反，请联系当地野生动物康复中心寻求指导。您可以通过立即动物帮助找到附近的资源。

articles.title: Can math stay human in the age of AI?
articles.author: Kathryn Hulick

paras.en: “Exponentially exploding,” mathematician Thomas Bloom told me by phone, describing the flood of new results in his field. Little did he know that hours later, OpenAI was going to post 722 mathematical manuscripts an unreleased AI model had produced.
paras.zh: “呈指数级爆炸式增长，”数学家托马斯·布鲁姆在电话中告诉我，他描述了他的领域中大量的新成果。他几乎不知道几个小时后，OpenAI 将发布 722 份由未发布的 AI 模型生成的数学手稿。

paras.en: The firehose of new work lends new urgency to the question: How is AI changing mathematical discovery? In their race for headline-grabbing breakthroughs, AI companies typically do not disclose their methods and data. That competition among AI companies threatens to overwhelm human collaboration and understanding.
paras.zh: 新研究的涌现给这个问题带来了新的紧迫性：人工智能如何改变数学发现？在争夺引人注目的突破的竞赛中，人工智能公司通常不会透露他们的方法和数据。人工智能公司之间的竞争可能会压倒人类的协作和理解。

paras.en: This tension had been playing out in miniature on a website Bloom runs that tracks progress on more than 1,000 problems originally posed and collected by Paul Erdős, one of the 20th century’s most prolific mathematicians. Here, people used to collaborate to discuss open problems, or ones for which the best solution either hasn’t been found or isn’t known to the greater math community. But increasingly, visitors were competing to close open problems with AI proofs that they often didn’t understand. Bloom, a mathematician at the University of Manchester in England, doesn’t want to spend his days refereeing AI-generated work. So, soon after we spoke, and before he knew that OpenAI would be announcing its latest results, Bloom posted that he’d no longer tag problems as open or solved, and he also closed comments.
paras.zh: 这种紧张局势在布鲁姆运营的一个网站上得到了缩影，该网站跟踪了 20 世纪最多产的数学家之一保罗·埃尔多斯 (Paul Erdős) 最初提出和收集的 1000 多个问题的进展情况。在这里，人们过去常常合作讨论未解决的问题，或者尚未找到或不为更大的数学界所知的最佳解决方案的问题。但越来越多的访问者竞相用他们通常不理解的人工智能证明来解决未解决的问题。布鲁姆是英国曼彻斯特大学的数学家，他不想把时间花在评审人工智能生成的工作上。因此，在我们交谈后不久，在他知道 OpenAI 将宣布其最新结果之前，Bloom 发帖表示，他不会再将问题标记为“开放”或“已解决”，并且他还关闭了评论。

paras.en: It’s definitely exciting that AI can tackle so many open problems so quickly. But can it help mathematicians understand the answers and build on them?
paras.zh: 人工智能能够如此迅速地解决如此多的开放性问题，这绝对令人兴奋。但它能帮助数学家理解答案并以此为基础吗？

paras.en: Just two days after OpenAI’s deluge of results, the peer-reviewed edition of a Google DeepMind study became public. First reported in a preprint earlier this year, it offers an inside look at how one AI system tackles open math problems. The system called AlphaProof Nexus solved 9 Erdős problems and made a number of other interesting mathematical advances, researchers report October 8 in Science.
paras.zh: 就在 OpenAI 发布大量结果两天后，谷歌 DeepMind 研究的同行评审版就公开了。它于今年早些时候在预印本中首次报道，它提供了人工智能系统如何解决开放数学问题的内部视角。研究人员 10 月 8 日在《科学》杂志上报道称，这个名为 AlphaProof Nexus 的系统解决了 9 个 Erdős 问题，并取得了许多其他有趣的数学进展。

paras.en: The report includes a detailed description of how the results were obtained. Plus, human mathematicians vetted many of the proofs. That’s “quite different” from how OpenAI and Anthropic are handling their math results, Bloom says.
paras.zh: 该报告详细描述了如何获得结果。另外，人类数学家审查了许多证明。布鲁姆说，这与 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 处理数学结果的方式“完全不同”。

paras.en: “The ultimate objective of any AI for math research,” says research scientist and study co-author Swarat Chaudhuri of Google DeepMind in London, should be “to advance mathematics as done by human mathematicians.”
paras.zh: 伦敦谷歌 DeepMind 的研究科学家兼研究合著者斯瓦拉特·乔杜里 (Swarat Chaudhuri) 表示：“任何人工智能用于数学研究的最终目标都应该是“像人类数学家一样推进数学发展”。

paras.en: In the recently published study Chaudhuri and his colleagues tested different configurations of their system. To tackle a collection of 353 open Erdős problems, they used multiple agents powered by the Gemini language model. These could call on AlphaProof, an AI model specially trained to do math, and the inspiration for the name of the overall system, for difficult steps. The agents also relied on Lean, math software that identifies steps that remain unproven, to check their logic. The agents shared their work, circulating promising proof attempts and discarding ones that weren’t going well.
paras.zh: 在最近发表的研究中，Chaudhuri 和他的同事测试了他们系统的不同配置。为了解决 353 个开放式 Erdős 问题，他们使用了由 Gemini 语言模型支持的多个代理。这些可以调用 AlphaProof，一种专门训练用于数学计算的人工智能模型，以及整个系统名称的灵感，以解决困难的步骤。特工们还依靠精益数学软件来识别尚未证实的步骤，以检查他们的逻辑。特工们分享了他们的工作，传播有希望的证明尝试，并放弃那些进展不顺利的尝试。

paras.en: The team also tested a simpler setup on the nine problems the full system solved. Independent Gemini agents worked through proofs using Lean’s feedback, without sharing attempts or consulting AlphaProof. That setup solved all nine, too. It was cheaper—using fewer computing resources—than the full system on easy problems and more expensive on the two toughest ones. The team did not establish whether the simpler setup would solve any of the problems the full system had missed.
paras.zh: 该团队还针对整个系统解决的九个问题测试了更简单的设置。独立的 Gemini 代理使用 Lean 的反馈完成了证明，没有分享尝试或咨询 AlphaProof。该设置也解决了所有九个问题。对于简单的问题，它比完整的系统更便宜（使用更少的计算资源），而对于两个最棘手的问题则更昂贵。该团队尚未确定更简单的设置是否可以解决整个系统遗漏的任何问题。

paras.en: The fact that the simpler setup could solve the same nine problems as the full system surprised Chaudhuri. It suggests that increasingly capable language models can tackle research mathematics with relatively simple checking tools.
paras.zh: 事实上，更简单的设置可以解决与完整系统相同的九个问题，这让 Chaudhuri 感到惊讶。它表明功能日益强大的语言模型可以使用相对简单的检查工具来解决研究数学问题。

paras.en: But computer-checking comes with a caveat. Lean checks only the statement it’s given, as it is written in its code. And a mathematical statement may be incorrectly translated to or from Lean code. An October 6 preprint shows why this translation matters. In the paper, the researchers pinpoint mismatches between parts of OpenAI’s written Navier–Stokes proof and its Lean counterpart. The mismatches do not mean the written proof is wrong, the team writes, but they note that a valid Lean proof does not automatically validate an AI-generated math paper.
paras.zh: 但计算机检查有一个警告。精益仅检查其给出的语句，正如其代码中所写的那样。数学陈述可能会被错误地翻译成精益代码或从精益代码中翻译出来。 10 月 6 日的预印本说明了此翻译的重要性。在论文中，研究人员查明了 OpenAI 书面的纳维-斯托克斯证明与其精益对应部分之间的不匹配之处。该团队写道，不匹配并不意味着书面证明是错误的，但他们指出，有效的精益证明不会自动验证人工智能生成的数学论文。

paras.en: That’s why the vetting human mathematicians did for the DeepMind publication is so important. “The human mathematician has to really think through the problem and set goals for the system,” Chaudhuri says. And even if the system failed to finish a proof, its checked steps helped mathematicians focus on the remaining gaps. “Math is ultimately a human art,” Chaudhuri says. “The system enhances the human user’s insights, and the human user is able to guide the system with new ideas.”
paras.zh: 这就是为什么人类数学家为 DeepMind 出版物所做的审查如此重要。 “人类数学家必须真正思考问题并为系统设定目标，”乔胡里说。即使系统未能完成证明，其检查步骤也可以帮助数学家专注于剩余的空白。 “数学归根结底是一门人类艺术，”乔胡里说。 “该系统增强了人类用户的洞察力，并且人类用户能够用新的想法来指导系统。”

paras.en: The mathematical results that the AlphaProof Nexus system achieved are “not really at the top level of importance,” says Bloom, who wasn’t involved with the work. But that underscores the team’s more measured approach. Google DeepMind, he says, is “trying to be more responsible with the science,” while companies like OpenAI are using math to showcase their software. OpenAI’s papers and accompanying Lean proofs were entirely AI-generated, leaving it up to the math community to work out what’s useful or useless.
paras.zh: 未参与这项工作的 Bloom 表示，AlphaProof Nexus 系统取得的数学结果“并不是真正重要的”。但这凸显了该团队更加谨慎的方法。他说，谷歌 DeepMind 正在“努力对科学更加负责”，而 OpenAI 等公司正在使用数学来展示他们的软件。 OpenAI 的论文和随附的精益证明完全由人工智能生成，由数学界来决定什么有用或无用。

paras.en: OpenAI says they worked with an independent advisory group to develop best practices on how to share their AI math results. But that group has said their advice was to not test unreleased AI models on advanced math, guidance the company clearly ignored.
paras.zh: OpenAI 表示，他们与一个独立咨询小组合作，开发了如何分享人工智能数学结果的最佳实践。但该组织表示，他们的建议是不要在高等数学上测试未发布的人工智能模型，而该公司显然忽视了这一指导。

paras.en: The company’s fast-moving, competitive approach continues to alienate mathematicians such as Bryna Kra of Northwestern University in Evanston, Ill. She says the company made some improvements in their efforts to cite past literature. And she’s excited about AI’s potential to solve important problems in math. But there is widespread concern, she says, that AI models have accessed people’s unpublished work. “We had a healthy, collaborative, sharing culture that is being destroyed,” she says. “Now, people are wary of sharing their ideas.”
paras.zh: 该公司快速发展、竞争性的做法继续疏远了伊利诺伊州埃文斯顿西北大学的 Bryna Kra 等数学家。她表示，该公司在引用过去文献方面做出了一些改进。她对人工智能解决重要数学问题的潜力感到兴奋。但她表示，人们普遍担心人工智能模型已经获取了人们未发表的作品。 “我们拥有健康、协作、分享的文化，但现在正在被破坏，”她说。 “现在，人们对分享自己的想法持谨慎态度。”

paras.en: Not all mathematicians feel this way about AI. The technology is “making math more accessible,” says Andrew Turner, who wonders why a small group of mathematicians should get to decide how we solve problems. Turner, who studied math and physics and is Now CTO of the company Plasma AI, based in New York City thinks “math is becoming engineering.” And doing math with machines will allow people to “answer questions previously unfathomable.”
paras.zh: 并非所有数学家都对人工智能有这样的看法。安德鲁·特纳说，这项技术“让数学变得更容易理解”，他想知道为什么一小群数学家应该决定我们如何解决问题。特纳学习了数学和物理，现任纽约 Plasma AI 公司的首席技术官，他认为“数学正在成为工程学”。用机器做数学将使人们能够“回答以前难以理解的问题”。

paras.en: A few days after Bloom shut down the competition on his website, Plasma AI announced a new website to track progress on Erdős problems. They will welcome AI results.
paras.zh: Bloom 关闭其网站上的竞赛几天后，Plasma AI 宣布建立一个新网站来跟踪 Erdős 问题的进展情况。他们会欢迎人工智能的结果。

paras.en: Bloom doesn’t see math as a Silicon Valley–esque move-fast-and-break-things competition. I agree, and hope that curious people will continue to explore problems they care about, with AI helping rather than taking over. At the end of his post announcing the changes to his website, Bloom wrote something that makes me tear up every time I read it. I hope everyone, even the most enthusiastic AI users, can find the time for this type of work: “Be confused, be stuck, be inspired. Find a messy proof, then find a better one,” he wrote. “Get tired, get hungry, get into a flow state. Argue, laugh, give up, drink some coffee and attack it again. Be human. Let your brain be open.”
paras.zh: 布鲁姆并不认为数学是硅谷式的快速行动、打破常规的竞赛。我同意，并希望好奇的人们能够继续探索他们关心的问题，让人工智能提供帮助而不是接管。在宣布网站变更的帖子的最后，布鲁姆写了一些让我每次读到都会流泪的东西。我希望每个人，甚至是最热情的人工智能用户，都能找到时间进行此类工作：“感到困惑，陷入困境，受到启发。找到一个混乱的证明，然后找到一个更好的证明，”他写道。 “累了，饿了，进入心流状态。争论，大笑，放弃，喝点咖啡，然后再次攻击它。做人。让你的大脑开放。”

articles.title: Artemis II results show how much science people can do at the moon
articles.author: Lisa Grossman

paras.en: Six months after the Artemis II mission sent four astronauts around the moon, the value of their closeup view is coming into focus. The first science results, released on October 7, reveal details of the moon’s array of colors, how often it gets hit by tiny rocks and lessons for squeezing as much science as possible out of future human lunar missions.
paras.zh: 在阿耳忒弥斯二号任务将四名宇航员送上月球六个月后，他们的特写镜头的价值开始受到人们的关注。第一批科学成果于 10 月 7 日发布，揭示了月球颜色排列的细节、月球被微小岩石撞击的频率，以及在未来人类登月任务中尽可能多地利用科学知识的经验教训。

paras.en: “We worked extremely hard to make sure we were able to maximize lunar science return from wherever we could in this mission,” said Artemis II flight science operations lead Kelsey Young at a virtual Lunar Surface Science Workshop meeting on October 7. “This is creating yet another tool in our toolbox as planetary scientists to understand our moon, our solar system, even our own planet.”
paras.zh: 10 月 7 日，阿耳忒弥斯二号飞行科学运营负责人凯尔西·杨 (Kelsey Young) 在一次虚拟的月球表面科学研讨会会议上表示：“我们非常努力地工作，以确保在这次任务中我们能够从任何可能的地方获得最大的月球科学回报。”“这为我们的行星科学家的工具箱中创建了另一个工具，以了解我们的月球、太阳系，甚至我们自己的星球。”

paras.en: NASA’s Artemis II mission sent four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon in April — the first time humans had been anywhere near our natural satellite in more than 50 years. Astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen spent about seven hours in close proximity to the moon taking scientific observations, describing the moon’s surprising colors and textures and witnessing a solar eclipse from space.
paras.zh: 今年 4 月，美国宇航局的阿耳忒弥斯二号任务派出四名宇航员进行了为期 10 天的绕月之旅，这是 50 多年来人类首次接近我们的天然卫星。宇航员里德·怀斯曼（Reid Wiseman）、维克多·格洛弗（Victor Glover）、克里斯蒂娜·科赫（Christina Koch）和杰里米·汉森（Jeremy Hansen）在月球附近进行了大约七个小时的科学观测，描述了月球令人惊讶的颜色和纹理，并从太空目睹了日食。

paras.en: Almost all of that event was livestreamed. But the astronauts took thousands of photos, notes and audio recordings that weren’t immediately made public. Part of the science team’s job was to digest those observations and release the data to anyone who wants to study them within six months of splashdown on April 10.
paras.zh: 几乎所有活动都进行了现场直播。但宇航员拍摄了数千张照片、笔记和录音，这些照片、笔记和录音并未立即公开。科学团队的部分工作是消化这些观察结果，并在 4 月 10 日溅落后的六个月内向任何想要研究这些数据的人发布数据。

paras.en: With three days to spare, the team released three reports and a massive data archive on October 7, the 67th anniversary of when the Soviet Luna 3 spacecraft took the first photograph of the farside of the moon. The results offer a rare test of what trained human observers can add to lunar research and what NASA can learn for future missions to the lunar surface.
paras.zh: 10 月 7 日是苏联月球 3 号宇宙飞船拍摄第一张月球背面照片 67 周年，利用三天的时间，该团队发布了三份报告和大量数据档案。这些结果提供了一次罕见的测试，检验训练有素的人类观察者可以为月球研究添加什么，以及美国宇航局可以为未来的月球表面任务学到什么。

paras.en: “We’re really excited to release all of this data,” earth scientist Sara Schmidt of NASA Johnson Space flight Cener in Houston said during the meeting. After six months of hard work, “this is enabling science to happen for the next, I don’t know, 60 years, if not more.”
paras.zh: “我们非常高兴能够发布所有这些数据，”休斯敦美国宇航局约翰逊太空飞行中心的地球科学家萨拉·施密特在会议上说道。经过六个月的努力，“这将使科学在未来，我不知道，60 年，甚至更长时间内继续发展。”

paras.en: How astronauts learn to observe the moon
paras.zh: 宇航员如何学习观察月球

paras.en: Surprisingly, the most valuable data from the mission were not the mind-blowingly gorgeous photos, but the astronauts’ verbal and written descriptions of what they were seeing.
paras.zh: 令人惊讶的是，这次任务中最有价值的数据并不是令人惊叹的华丽照片，而是宇航员对所见事物的口头和书面描述。

paras.en: Before launch, the astronauts had extensive training in lunar geology and science observations. They were an extension of the science team, said field geologist Cindy Evans also of NASA Johnson Space Flight Center, one of the astronauts’ instructors.
paras.zh: 在发射之前，宇航员接受了月球地质学和科学观测方面的广泛培训。美国宇航局约翰逊太空飞行中心的现场地质学家辛迪·埃文斯（Cindy Evans）是宇航员的教练之一，他说，他们是科学团队的延伸。

paras.en: “You could hear it in their voices. They understood the language of geology,” she said.
paras.zh: “你可以从他们的声音中听到这一点。他们懂得地质学的语言，”她说。

paras.en: That training was meant to help answer a question Young hears often: What can humans add that a camera can’t?
paras.zh: 这项训练旨在帮助回答杨经常听到的一个问题：人类可以添加哪些相机不能添加的内容？

paras.en: During the flyby, the astronauts worked in pairs. Two of them spoke to mission control on the ground, giving periodic updates to the science team on what they were seeing. The other two recorded themselves describing their observations and reactions and used a stylus to annotate specially made maps of the moon that had been uploaded to their tablets during flight. Those notes, doodles and recordings were not made public until now.
paras.zh: 在飞越过程中，宇航员两人一组工作。其中两人与地面任务控制中心进行了交谈，定期向科学团队通报他们所看到的情况。另外两人记录了自己的观察和反应，并使用手写笔注释了特制的月球地图，这些地图在飞行过程中上传到了他们的平板电脑上。这些笔记、涂鸦和录音直到现在才被公开。

paras.en: The idea was to give the crew high tech field notebooks, Young says.
paras.zh: 杨说，这个想法是为船员提供高科技野外笔记本。

paras.en: “If you have any field experience, you know your field notebook is your best friend,” she said in the meeting. On Earth, geologists capture nuance and context in written and spoken words, as well as sketches, she said. “We wanted to provide the ability to capture that nuanced information from the crew.”
paras.zh: “如果你有任何现场经验，你就会知道你的现场笔记本是你最好的朋友，”她在会议上说。她说，在地球上，地质学家通过书面和口头文字以及草图捕捉细微差别和背景。 “我们希望提供从机组人员那里捕获细微信息的能力。”

paras.en: One example of this was when Koch sketched her view of the Orientale basin, detailing differences in texture and layers around the crater.
paras.zh: 其中一个例子是科赫描绘了她对东方盆地的看法，详细描述了火山口周围纹理和层次的差异。

paras.en: “Sketches can be so powerful,” Young says. “They’re quick and dirty and that’s exactly the right thing to do. You’re capturing that nuance really quickly before it leaves your brain.”
paras.zh: “草图可以如此强大，”杨说。 “它们又快又脏，这正是正确的做法。在它离开你的大脑之前，你很快就能捕捉到这种细微差别。”

paras.en: Some of the most unique observations came during the 54 minutes when the moon eclipsed the sun, giving the astronauts a view of the solar corona, interplanetary dust and other stars and planets. That was a favorite moment for planetary scientist Jennifer Heldmann of NASA’s Ames Research Center in California.
paras.zh: 一些最独特的观测发生在月球遮住太阳的 54 分钟期间，宇航员可以看到日冕、行星际尘埃以及其他恒星和行星。这是美国宇航局加利福尼亚州艾姆斯研究中心的行星科学家詹妮弗·赫尔德曼最喜欢的时刻。

paras.en: “That audio showed their sheer joy and amazement in what they were seeing and where they were,” Heldmann says. “They were so blown away by what they were seeing, while also taking very relevant science observations.”
paras.zh: “这段音频显示了他们对所看到的事物和所在位置的纯粹的喜悦和惊讶，”赫尔德曼说。 “他们对所看到的一切感到非常震惊，同时也进行了非常相关的科学观察。”

paras.en: But some of the most affecting moments were when words failed. When Glover and Koch saw the Earth emerge from behind the moon, for a while all they could say was “Oh my gosh!”
paras.zh: 但一些最感人的时刻是言语无法表达的时候。当格洛弗和科赫看到地球从月球后面出现时，有一段时间他们只能说“天哪！”

paras.en: “I guess I should be trying to describe it, but I mean, good grief,” Glover’s tablet recorded him saying.
paras.zh: “我想我应该尝试描述一下，但我的意思是，天哪，”格洛弗的平板电脑记录了他的说法。

paras.en: “No, I tried, but it’s impossible,” Koch agreed. “You might be able to fly a spaceship and talk, but if you can see that and talk, you just ain’t right.”
paras.zh: “不，我试过了，但这是不可能的，”科赫同意道。 “你也许能够驾驶宇宙飞船并说话，但如果你能看到它并说话，那你就是不对的。”

paras.en: Astronauts spotted tiny impacts on the moon
paras.zh: 宇航员发现月球上的微小撞击

paras.en: Another thing the astronauts were able to see during the eclipse were impact flashes — tiny blips of light marking where bits of rock hit the moon.
paras.zh: 宇航员在日食期间能够看到的另一件事是撞击闪光——微小的光点标志着岩石碎片撞击月球的位置。

paras.en: “It’s a pinpoint of light,” Hansen said in his recorded observations. “It’s not like a meteor, you didn’t see anything else, it’s just like a bloop.”
paras.zh: “这是一个精确的光点，”汉森在他的观察记录中说道。 “它不像流星，你没有看到任何其他东西，它只是像一个斑点。”

paras.en: Before launch, the science team identified and prioritized observations they hoped the crew would be able to make during the flyby. Impact flashes were at the top of the list. Seeing the flashes would give scientists a way to estimate how often the moon is struck by incoming rocks, and how large those rocks are. That’s an important thing to know for protecting future missions where astronauts will walk on the surface or build a long-term moon base.
paras.zh: 在发射之前，科学团队确定了他们希望机组人员在飞越过程中能够进行的观察结果并确定了优先顺序。冲击闪光位居榜首。看到闪光将使科学家能够估计月球被撞击岩石的频率以及这些岩石有多大。对于保护宇航员在月球表面行走或建立长期月球基地的未来任务来说，了解这一点非常重要。

paras.en: Scientists didn’t know whether the astronauts would see any flashes at all. They saw five. The flashes were “pinpricks of light lasting less than a second, with no color associated with the flash,” Heldmann said at the meeting.
paras.zh: 科学家们根本不知道宇航员是否会看到任何闪光。他们看到了五个。赫尔德曼在会议上说，这些闪光是“持续时间不到一秒的针刺光，没有与闪光相关的颜色”。

paras.en: Comparing the number of flashes per minute to theoretical models of how many impacts the moon might experience, scientists determined that the incoming rocks were tiny, about 8.5 grams and just over 4.5 centimeters across — about the size of a golf ball.
paras.zh: 通过将每分钟的闪光次数与月球可能经历的撞击次数的理论模型进行比较，科学家们确定，传入的岩石很小，约为 8.5 克，直径略多于 4.5 厘米，大约相当于高尔夫球的大小。

paras.en: “With these observations, we believe that the Artemis II crew set a record for the smallest meteorites ever optically observed to impact the moon,” Heldmann said.
paras.zh: 赫尔德曼说：“通过这些观察，我们相信阿耳忒弥斯二号机组人员创造了有史以来光学观测到撞击月球的最小陨石的记录。”

paras.en: The resulting craters are probably less than a meter wide, too small for cameras on NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter to see.
paras.zh: 由此产生的陨石坑可能不到一米宽，对于美国宇航局月球勘测轨道飞行器上的相机来说太小了。

paras.en: That’s good news for future astronauts. Artemis IV, planned for 2028, is supposed to bring astronauts to the lunar surface for the first time since Apollo. If successful, it will be a two-week mission using landers from spaceflight companies Blue Origin or SpaceX. The probability of dangerous impact during such a mission is less than 1 in 10 million, Heldmann said. For a larger moon base meant to last a decade, the probability is higher, but still low.
paras.zh: 这对未来的宇航员来说是个好消息。计划于 2028 年进行的阿耳忒弥斯四号计划将继阿波罗计划之后首次将宇航员送上月球表面。如果成功，这将是一次为期两周的任务，使用航天公司 Blue Origin 或 SpaceX 的着陆器。赫尔德曼说，在此类任务中发生危险撞击的可能性小于千万分之一。对于一个打算持续十年的更大的月球基地来说，可能性更高，但仍然很低。

paras.en: “Now we can start to quantify those impact probabilities, which turns out are very very low,” she says. “Crews will be very safe.”
paras.zh: “现在我们可以开始量化这些影响概率，结果证明这些概率非常非常低，”她说。 “工作人员将会非常安全。”

paras.en: The moon’s muted colors were another high-priority observation for the science team. Lunar hues and brightnesses can change with terrain roughness, surface temperature and mineralogy — and they’re much more discernable with human eyes than with cameras. The crew also saw how colors changed as the viewing angle and light levels changed.
paras.zh: 月亮的柔和颜色是科学团队的另一个高度优先的观测。月球的色调和亮度会随着地形粗糙度、表面温度和矿物学的变化而变化——而且人眼比相机更容易辨别它们。工作人员还看到颜色如何随着视角和光照水平的变化而变化。

paras.en: “This is such a cool demonstration of the value of human eyes as scientific sensors,” said planetary scientist Ariel Deutsch, also of NASA Ames.
paras.zh: “这非常酷地证明了人眼作为科学传感器的价值，”同样来自美国宇航局艾姆斯研究中心的行星科学家阿里尔·多伊奇 (Ariel Deutsch) 说道。

paras.en: Combining the crew’s observations with other data going back to the 1970s let scientists connect colors to composition. Blues were associated with titanium-rich volcanic rocks. Browns reflect different iron levels. Greens are from glass formed during volcanic eruptions or asteroid impacts.
paras.zh: 将机组人员的观察结果与 20 世纪 70 年代的其他数据相结合，科学家们将颜色与构图联系起来。蓝色与富含钛的火山岩有关。棕色反映了不同的铁含量。绿色是由火山爆发或小行星撞击期间形成的玻璃制成的。

paras.en: Future astronauts could use this information to create terrain maps and to find specific materials on the moon for sample collection or resources.
paras.zh: 未来的宇航员可以利用这些信息来创建地形图，并在月球上寻找特定材料以收集样本或资源。

paras.en: The crew also was enamored with the terminator, the boundary between light and dark, which revealed lunar topography in a new way.
paras.zh: 船员们还着迷于“明暗界限”，它以一种新的方式揭示了月球的地形。

paras.en: “Even as rugged as the far side looks … man, when you look at the terminator, it is just, like, impossibly rugged,” Wiseman said during the flight. “And it reminds you that the whole farside is that way. It’s just the terminator is really bringing out the shadows and the hills and the valleys. And it is just — it’s unbelievable.”
paras.zh: 怀斯曼在飞行过程中说：“即使远方看起来很崎岖……伙计，当你看终结者时，它就像是难以置信的崎岖不平。” “它提醒你，整个远端都是那样的。只是终结者真正带出了阴影、丘陵和山谷。这只是——这令人难以置信。”

paras.en: The lighting at the terminator is similar to what future astronauts might expect at the moon’s south pole, where the sun will be low on the horizon and may cast dramatic shadows.
paras.zh: 明暗界线处的照明类似于未来宇航员在月球南极所期望的照明，在那里太阳将位于地平线下方，并可能投射出戏剧性的阴影。

paras.en: “We want to make sure we have a good handle on that for both science and operations and exploration,” Heldmann said.
paras.zh: 赫尔德曼说：“我们希望确保我们能够很好地处理科学、运营和勘探方面的问题。”

paras.en: What Artemis II taught NASA for future moon missions
paras.zh: 阿耳忒弥斯二号教会了美国宇航局未来的月球任务

paras.en: With the lessons from Artemis II in hand, now it’s the next astronauts’ turn.
paras.zh: 有了阿尔忒弥斯二号的经验教训，现在轮到下一位宇航员了。

paras.en: Some recommendations coming out of Artemis II focus on improving conditions in the spacecraft and weaving science into mission planning better. For example, due to time constraints, the astronauts’ cameras were not calibrated before flight. The team is now trying to calibrate them back on Earth, but it can’t re-create how the windows affected images because the windows were charred on the way back through Earth’s atmosphere.
paras.zh: 阿耳忒弥斯二号提出的一些建议侧重于改善航天器的条件，并将科学更好地融入任务规划中。例如，由于时间限制，宇航员的相机在飞行前没有进行校准。该团队现在正试图在地球上校准它们，但无法重现窗户如何影响图像，因为窗户在返回地球大气层的途中被烧焦。

paras.en: Another takeaway from Artemis II is to continue to refine and train astronauts in descriptive notetaking. The audio notes will be even more important for the first landed missions, where astronauts in spacesuits will not be able to write in a notebook.
paras.zh: 阿耳忒弥斯二号的另一个收获是继续完善和训练宇航员进行描述性笔记。对于第一次着陆任务来说，音频笔记将更加重要，因为穿着宇航服的宇航员将无法在笔记本上书写。

paras.en: “We want to train astronauts to be field scientists, regardless of the landing site, regardless of the mission that they’re given,” Young says.
paras.zh: “我们希望将宇航员训练成现场科学家，无论着陆地点如何，无论他们承担的任务是什么，”杨说。

paras.en: The buddy system of two astronauts at the windows, two talking to the ground, led to better science, the team concluded.
paras.zh: 研究小组得出结论，两名宇航员在窗户旁、两人与地面交谈的伙伴系统带来了更好的科学结果。

paras.en: “The crew had scientific discussions and tried to understand what they were viewing,” Heldmann says. For surface missions, where time is limited and choices must be made quickly, that collaboration will be even more important.
paras.zh: “工作人员进行了科学讨论，并试图了解他们所看到的内容，”赫尔德曼说。对于时间有限且必须快速做出选择的地面任务，协作将更加重要。

paras.en: The crew also commented on how helpful it was.
paras.zh: 工作人员还评论说它有多么有帮助。

paras.en: “When we actually do go down there to the surface, I know for safety reasons that we would never send someone alone, but I just want to really emphasize how important the discussion time was,” Glover said. “When we started to talk, we not only got better science discussion, we got better human connection.”
paras.zh: “当我们真正到地面时，我知道出于安全原因，我们永远不会单独派人，但我只是想真正强调讨论时间的重要性，”格洛弗说。 “当我们开始交谈时，我们不仅得到了更好的科学讨论，而且得到了更好的人际关系。”

articles.title: Horned dinosaurs’ weapons evolved to handle the forces of combat
articles.author: Jake Buehler

paras.en: Triceratops’ massive skulls were built for horn-to-horn grappling. The rhino-like Centrosaurus could withstand stabbing its nose horn up and down. And the parrot-faced Psittacosaurus would have been wise to avoid a fight: Its head was ill-suited to handle blows.
paras.zh: 三角龙巨大的头骨是为角对角格斗而建造的。像犀牛一样的尖角龙可以承受上下刺伤它的鼻角。鹦鹉嘴龙应该明智地避免战斗：它的头部不适合承受打击。

paras.en: New simulations using 3-D models of the heads of five different horned dinosaurs reveal what forces the skulls could withstand in battle. The results provide insight into how these dinosaurs evolved to use their face-based armory in combat, researchers report September 24 in PeerJ.
paras.zh: 使用五种不同有角恐龙头部的 3D 模型进行的新模拟揭示了头骨在战斗中可以承受的力量。研究人员于 9 月 24 日在 PeerJ 上发表报告称，这些结果让我们深入了解这些恐龙如何进化到在战斗中使用基于面部的军械库。

paras.en: Ceratopsians — horned dinosaurs like Triceratops — have been hypothesized to use their imposing headgear as armaments for battling with other members of the species.
paras.zh: 角龙——像三角龙一样有角的恐龙——被认为会使用它们雄伟的头饰作为与该物种其他成员战斗的武器。

paras.en: Fossilized facial injuries consistent with head-to-head violence have provided physical clues. “We know from many fossils that ceratopsian skulls tended to get banged up a little bit … in very particular spots on the frill or on the cheek,” says Andrew Farke, a paleontologist at Raymond M. Alf Museum of Paleontology in Claremont, California. But little else was known about how ceratopsians actually used their horns in battle.
paras.zh: 与头对头暴力相符的面部损伤化石提供了物理线索。 “我们从许多化石中得知，角龙的头骨往往会受到一点撞击……特别是在褶边或脸颊上的特定位置，”加利福尼亚州克莱蒙特市雷蒙德·M·阿尔夫古生物学博物馆的古生物学家安德鲁·法克说。但人们对角龙在战斗中如何实际使用它们的角知之甚少。

paras.en: Studying the biomechanics of the animals’ weaponized skulls could provide information on what movements and forces the dinosaurs evolved to tolerate. Such biomechanics research had previously been done on the bite stresses of theropod dinosaurs like Tyrannosaurus and on the forces felt by the club tails of armored dinosaurs, says vertebrate paleontologist Eric Austin Ames Jr.
paras.zh: 研究动物武器化头骨的生物力学可以提供有关恐龙进化到能够承受哪些运动和力量的信息。脊椎动物古生物学家小埃里克·奥斯汀·艾姆斯 (Eric Austin Ames Jr.) 表示，此类生物力学研究以前是针对暴龙等兽脚亚目恐龙的咬合应力以及装甲恐龙的棒尾所感受到的力进行的。

paras.en: Ames and his colleagues at the University of Bristol in England developed digital 3-D models of six skulls across five ceratopsian species spread across the group’s evolutionary tree. They simulated the combat stress experienced across the skull, varying the direction of attack and how the weaponry was used. Higher stresses in the skull meant a greater risk of mechanical failure, Ames says. The dinosaurs are more likely to have evolved to fight in a way that was well-tolerated by the skull’s mechanics.
paras.zh: 艾姆斯和他在英国布里斯托大学的同事开发了数字 3D 模型，其中包含五个角龙物种的六个头骨，这些物种分布在该群体的进化树上。他们模拟了头骨上所经历的战斗压力，改变了攻击方向和武器的使用方式。艾姆斯说，头骨中的应力越高，机械故障的风险就越大。恐龙更有可能进化成一种头骨结构能够很好耐受的战斗方式。

paras.en: The team found that early members of the group from about 125 million years ago — like the hornless, husky-sized Psittacosaurus — didn’t have skulls well-suited for combat of any type. The pig-sized Protoceratops had a skull that tolerated ramming fairly well. Larger, later-diverging species like Centrosaurus and the three-horned Triceratops and Spiclypeus appeared adapted to a wider range of combat styles.
paras.zh: 研究小组发现，大约 1.25 亿年前该群体的早期成员——比如无角、体型哈士奇的鹦鹉嘴龙——没有适合任何类型战斗的头骨。猪大小的原角龙的头骨能够很好地承受撞击。较大的、后来分化的物种，如尖角龙、三角三角龙和尖角龙，似乎适应了更广泛的战斗风格。

paras.en: Centrosaurus may have been a specialized stabber, lunging its head to jab at opponents. “When we tested [the skull] with vertical forces, it actually handled the stresses really well,” Ames says. “But when we tried side-to-side, it did not perform very well.”In contrast, Triceratops and Spiclypeus had skulls that tolerate the forces generated by interlocking horns and wrestling.
paras.zh: 尖角龙可能是一种专门的刺伤者，用它的头刺向对手。 “当我们用垂直力测试[头骨]时，它实际上很好地处理了压力，”艾姆斯说。 “但当我们尝试并排时，它的表现并不是很好。”相比之下，三角龙和尖角龙的头骨可以承受角交错和摔跤产生的力量。

paras.en: Ames thinks ceratopsians’ horns and frills probably first evolved for social and sexual display, but were soon used for full contact purposes. “Throughout their evolutionary history, their [horns’ traits] started to really explode in diversity and that coincided with different intraspecific combat styles,” he says. “This is something we see in modern herbivores.”
paras.zh: 艾姆斯认为角龙的角和饰边可能最初是为了社交和性展示而进化的，但很快就被用于充分接触的目的。 “在它们的进化史上，它们的[角的特征]开始真正爆发出多样性，这与不同的种内战斗风格相吻合，”他说。 “这是我们在现代食草动物身上看到的。”

paras.en: Much like with the antlers and horns of modern deer, buffalo or antelope, these weapons could have easily been turned on predators as well. “These adaptations are kind of like a Swiss Army knife,” Ames says. “They can be used for multiple things.”
paras.zh: 就像现代鹿、水牛或羚羊的鹿角和角一样，这些武器也可以很容易地用来攻击掠食者。 “这些改编有点像瑞士军刀，”艾姆斯说。 “它们可以用于多种用途。”

paras.en: The team created its 3-D models from surface scans of fossilized skulls. More detailed models that better simulate the complicated internal structure of these dinosaurs’ immense, bizarre skulls could provide even more insight to this prehistoric fight club, Farke says.
paras.zh: 该团队根据头骨化石的表面扫描创建了 3D 模型。法克说，更详细的模型可以更好地模拟这些恐龙巨大而奇异的头骨的复杂内部结构，可以为这个史前搏击俱乐部提供更多的见解。

articles.title: New Genus of Nightmare Spaghetti Worms Found Deep Under The Indian Ocean
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: Just when you thought it was safe to enter the benthic depths of the Indian Ocean, a new eldritch horror emerges from the darkness.
paras.zh: 就在您认为可以安全进入印度洋海底深处时，黑暗中出现了新的恐怖恐怖。

paras.en: Hundreds of meters below the waves off the coasts of Christmas Island and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, scientists have found a whole new genus of seafloor-dwelling worms.
paras.zh: 在圣诞岛和科科斯（基林）群岛海岸海浪以下数百米处，科学家们发现了一种全新的海底蠕虫属。

paras.en: They're known as spaghetti worms, but their resemblance to delicious pasta is more of a nightmare variety – a horrible tangle of spaghetti-like tendrils writhing from a squishy body that spends its life sheltered inside a protective tube.
paras.zh: 它们被称为意大利面蠕虫，但它们与美味意大利面的相似之处更像是一种噩梦——一团可怕的意大利面状卷须从柔软的身体中扭动起来，一生都被保护在保护管内。

paras.en: It's that squishy body that makes the three species assigned to the new genus Terebellosuctoria stand out: On their undersides are modified pads that form strange, sucker-like structures unlike those of any other known genus of spaghetti worm.
paras.zh: 正是这种柔软的身体使属于新属 Terebellosuctoria 的三个物种脱颖而出：它们的底面有经过改造的肉垫，形成奇怪的吸盘状结构，与任何其他已知的意大利面条虫属不同。

paras.en: While the team of scientists that described the genus in a paper published in Records of the Australian Museum has some clues, the purpose of the suckers is something of a mystery.
paras.zh: 虽然在《澳大利亚博物馆记录》上发表的一篇论文中描述该属的科学家团队掌握了一些线索，但吸盘的用途仍然是个谜。

paras.en: They could be for sucking out the souls of drowned sailors, for all we know.
paras.zh: 据我们所知，它们可能是为了吸出溺水水手的灵魂。

paras.en: "The sucker-like structure is what makes this new genus so interesting and unique," says marine zoologist Elena Kupriyanova of the Australian Museum, the paper's first author.
paras.zh: 该论文的第一作者、澳大利亚博物馆的海洋动物学家埃琳娜·库普里亚诺娃（Elena Kupriyanova）说：“吸盘状结构使这个新属如此有趣和独特。”

paras.en: Actually, for all their somewhat alarming appearance outside of their habitat, spaghetti worms are relatively unassuming little creatures. Their family, Terebellidae, is related to earthworms, in fact – although the spaghetti worms' anatomy is significantly more baroque.
paras.zh: 事实上，尽管意大利面条虫在栖息地之外的外表有些令人担忧，但它们是相对不起眼​​的小生物。事实上，它们的家族（Terebellidae）与蚯蚓有亲缘关系——尽管意大利面条虫的解剖结构明显更加巴洛克式。

paras.en: They usually plonk themselves into the seabed, building a tube for protection, and extending their tentacles – the 'spaghetti' – to truffle out tasty morsels from the surrounding sediment.
paras.zh: 它们通常会潜入海底，建造一根管子进行保护，并伸出触手（“意大利面条”），从周围的沉积物中挖出美味的松饼。

paras.en: They're also not exclusive to the deep ocean. Many Terebellid worms live in shallower waters, and almost all Australian species described to date inhabit more sunlit depths.
paras.zh: 它们也并非深海独有。许多Terebellid蠕虫生活在较浅的水域中，迄今为止描述的几乎所有澳大利亚物种都栖息在阳光照射较多的深处。

paras.en: But our understanding of the life that inhabits deeper waters is significantly more limited than our knowledge of the shallows.
paras.zh: 但我们对深海生物的了解远比对浅海生物的了解要有限。

paras.en: During research voyages in 2021 and 2022, scientists aboard Australia's research vessel Investigator explored seamounts around Christmas Island and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, collecting specimens from these little-explored deep-sea ecosystems.
paras.zh: 在 2021 年和 2022 年的研究航行中，澳大利亚研究船“调查者”号上的科学家探索了圣诞岛和科科斯（基林）群岛周围的海山，从这些鲜为人知的深海生态系统中收集了标本。

paras.en: These voyages yielded many species totally new to science. Some have already been described. Others are still awaiting formal description.
paras.zh: 这些航行产生了许多对科学来说全新的物种。有些已经描述过。其他人仍在等待正式描述。

paras.en: But among the hundreds of specimens collected from the seafloor, two kinds of worms in particular stood out as unusual.
paras.zh: 但在从海底收集的数百个标本中，有两种蠕虫特别引人注目，显得异常异常。

paras.en: They were collected from seamounts at depths between 467 and 674 meters (1,532 and 2,211 feet), and, when extracted from their protective tubes, revealed sucker-like structures formed from modified pads on the undersides of the front portions of their segmented bodies.
paras.zh: 它们是从 467 至 674 米（1,532 至 2,211 英尺）深处的海山中采集的，当从保护管中取出时，会发现在其分段身体前部的下侧有由改良垫形成的吸盘状结构。

paras.en: One increasingly common step in describing a new species is to sequence its DNA.
paras.zh: 描述新物种的一个越来越常见的步骤是对其 DNA 进行测序。

paras.en: When the researchers analyzed the DNA of their peculiar worms, the evidence – combined with their distinctive anatomy – pointed to something even more exciting than two new species: an entirely new genus.
paras.zh: 当研究人员分析这些特殊蠕虫的 DNA 时，证据——结合它们独特的解剖结构——指出了比两个新物种更令人兴奋的东西：一个全新的属。

paras.en: That genus is Terebellosuctoria, a name that acknowledges their weird sucker-like structures, and the two species are Terebellosuctoria jimii and Terebellosuctoria keelingensis.
paras.zh: 该属是 Terebellosuctoria，这个名字承认了它们奇怪的吸盘状结构，这两个物种是 Terebellosuctoria jimii 和 Terebellosuctoria keelingensis。

paras.en: Eagle-eyed readers, however, will recall that we mentioned three species of Terebellosuctoria.
paras.zh: 然而，眼尖的读者会记得我们提到过三种 Terebellosuctoria。

paras.en: The third member of this strange little group had actually been discovered before – thousands of kilometers away, in even deeper waters (843 meters) off the coast of Japan.
paras.zh: 这个奇怪的小群体的第三个成员实际上以前就被发现过——在数千公里之外，在日本海岸附近更深的水域（843 米）。

paras.en: It was described in a 2025 paper, and tentatively assigned to the Lanice genus, named Lanice spongicola, but its unusual anatomy left its evolutionary relationships unresolved.
paras.zh: 它在 2025 年的一篇论文中进行了描述，并暂时归属于 Lanice 属，命名为 Lanice spongicola，但其不寻常的解剖结构使其进化关系尚未解决。

paras.en: The Japanese researchers had sequenced its DNA, too. Their analysis suggested that the worm was related to members of the Lanice and Loimia genera, but they couldn't confidently place it in either.
paras.zh: 日本研究人员也对其 DNA 进行了测序。他们的分析表明，这种蠕虫与 Lanice 属和 Loimia 属的成员有关，但他们不能自信地将其归入其中任何一个属。

paras.en: They even suggested that the discovery of other worms with similar sucker-like structures might reveal an entirely new evolutionary lineage.
paras.zh: 他们甚至认为，发现具有类似吸盘状结构的其他蠕虫可能会揭示一个全新的进化谱系。

paras.en: By comparing the anatomy and DNA of the Australian specimens with the Japanese species, Kupriyanova and her colleagues were able to resolve the mystery. Lanice spongicola has now been reassigned to the new genus as Terebellosuctoria spongicola.
paras.zh: 通过比较澳大利亚样本和日本物种的解剖结构和 DNA，库普里亚诺娃和她的同事们解开了这个谜团。 Lanice spongicola 现在已被重新分配到新属，称为 Terebellosuctoria spongicola。

paras.en: And there's one more intriguing clue about those mysterious suckers.
paras.zh: 关于这些神秘的吸盘，还有一个更有趣的线索。

paras.en: The Japanese researchers observed their worm using its sucker-like structure to cling to the inside of its tube, which was attached to a deep-sea glass sponge. They suggested that it might help anchor the animal in a habitat where loose sediment is scarce.
paras.zh: 日本研究人员观察到他们的蠕虫利用其吸盘状结构粘附在其管子的内部，该管子附着在深海玻璃海绵上。他们认为，这可能有助于将动物固定在松散沉积物稀缺的栖息地。

paras.en: Whether the Australian species use their suckers in the same way remains to be seen.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚物种是否以同样的方式使用吸盘还有待观察。

paras.en: But that may have to wait for another day. The voyage yielded many potential new discoveries. This particular paper detailed seven new species – the two spaghetti worms and five other annelids.
paras.zh: 但这可能还要再等一天。这次航行产生了许多潜在的新发现。这篇特别的论文详细介绍了七个新物种——两种意大利面蠕虫和其他五种环节动物。

paras.en: There are many more to go – and that's just from a relatively small patch of the deep ocean.
paras.zh: 还有更多的地方有待探索——而这只是来自深海相对较小的一块区域。

paras.en: "An expedition may collect hundreds or thousands of specimens, but discovering what they actually are can take years," Kupriyanova says.
paras.zh: “一次探险可能会收集数百或数千个标本，但发现它们的实际情况可能需要数年时间，”库普里亚诺娃说。

paras.en: "The specimens become part of museum research collections, where taxonomists can continue studying them long after the voyage has finished. The seven species described in this paper are another step in working through that remarkable archive."
paras.zh: “这些标本成为博物馆研究收藏的一部分，分类学家可以在航行结束后很长时间内继续研究它们。本文中描述的七个物种是研究这一非凡档案的又一步。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Records of the Australian Museum.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《澳大利亚博物馆记录》上。

articles.title: Brown Fat Can Be Beneficial For The Body – And a Blood Pressure Drug Could Turn It On
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: Body fat can bring health benefits as well as health problems, depending on where it is and how much of it there is.
paras.zh: 身体脂肪既可以带来健康益处，也可以带来健康问题，具体取决于它的位置和含量。

paras.en: Brown fat in particular is thought to be mostly good for us – burning up excess sugar and fat and regulating body temperature.
paras.zh: 尤其是棕色脂肪被认为对我们最有好处——燃烧多余的糖和脂肪并调节体温。

paras.en: In a new study in Nature, researchers led by a team from Rockefeller University in the US have presented more evidence for brown fat (adipose tissue) boosting not just physical health, but mental health too.
paras.zh: 在《自然》杂志上的一项新研究中，由美国洛克菲勒大学团队领导的研究人员提供了更多证据，证明棕色脂肪（脂肪组织）不仅可以促进身体健康，还可以促进心理健康。

paras.en: What's more, they've also identified a potential medication option: the blood pressure drug losartan was associated with a greater likelihood of having detectable brown fat in the study data.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，他们还确定了一种潜在的药物选择：血压药物氯沙坦在研究数据中与可检测到的棕色脂肪的可能性更大有关。

paras.en: All of these findings came from scanning the medical records of 101,243 study participants using AI to find brown fat, plus further tests in mouse models.
paras.zh: 所有这些发现都来自使用 AI 扫描 101,243 名研究参与者的医疗记录来寻找棕色脂肪，以及在小鼠模型中进行的进一步测试。

paras.en: "Our studies harnessing artificial intelligence and big data identify new clinical phenotypes linked to brown adipose tissue and serve as a platform for drug repurposing to activate this tissue in humans," write the researchers in their published paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在发表的论文中写道：“我们利用人工智能和大数据的研究确定了与棕色脂肪组织相关的新临床表型，并作为药物再利用的平台来激活人类的这种组织。”

paras.en: The first part of the research involved identifying nearly 8,900 of the study participants with detectable amounts of brown fat.
paras.zh: 研究的第一部分涉及识别近 8,900 名研究参与者是否含有可检测到的棕色脂肪。

paras.en: It's not something we all have in very large amounts, at least compared to the more common white fat: The level declines with age, and what brown fat we do have is often dormant.
paras.zh: 至少与更常见的白色脂肪相比，我们所有人都拥有大量的棕色脂肪：其水平随着年龄的增长而下降，而我们所拥有的棕色脂肪通常处于休眠状态。

paras.en: After crunching the numbers on these participants compared to matched controls, the researchers found that those with brown fat were significantly less likely to have type 2 diabetes or heart disease.
paras.zh: 在对这些参与者与匹配对照组的数据进行比较后，研究人员发现，那些拥有棕色脂肪的人患 2 型糖尿病或心脏病的可能性明显较低。

paras.en: Then there were the mental health findings – the brown fat group was also less likely to have anxiety or depression.
paras.zh: 然后是心理健康研究结果——棕色脂肪组也不太可能出现焦虑或抑郁。

paras.en: More 'active' brown fat meant greater benefits, with armpit fat showing the biggest links. The data doesn't show direct cause and effect, but there do appear to be notable associations found here that can be followed up on in future research.
paras.zh: 更多“活跃”的棕色脂肪意味着更大的好处，其中腋窝脂肪的联系最为显着。这些数据没有显示直接的因果关系，但这里似乎确实发现了显着的关联，可以在未来的研究中进行跟进。

paras.en: The researchers then moved on to blood pressure drugs. Another pattern that emerged was that people on blood pressure pills were more likely to have detectable levels of brown fat.
paras.zh: 研究人员随后转向降血压药物。出现的另一种模式是，服用降压药的人更有可能检测到棕色脂肪水平。

paras.en: Switching to tests on mice, the team found that animals given losartan had brown fat that was more active – burning more energy and producing more heat, although any subsequent health benefits still have to be determined.
paras.zh: 研究小组转而对小鼠进行测试，发现服用氯沙坦的动物的棕色脂肪更加活跃，燃烧更多的能量并产生更多的热量，尽管随后的健康益处仍有待确定。

paras.en: This activation was backed up by an analysis of brown fat cells in mice. It also happened via a different route to the one used to lower blood pressure, the study determined, which opens up more potential for future treatments.
paras.zh: 对小鼠棕色脂肪细胞的分析支持了这种激活。研究确定，它还通过与用于降低血压的途径不同的途径发生，这为未来的治疗开辟了更多潜力。

paras.en: "The fact that its different effects are mediated by different molecular pathways is advantageous, since it means we could potentially isolate them in future therapies," says endocrinologist Nicolás Gómez-Banoy from Rockefeller University.
paras.zh: 洛克菲勒大学的内分泌学家 Nicolás Gómez-Banoy 表示：“它的不同作用是由不同的分子途径介导的，这一事实是有利的，因为这意味着我们有可能在未来的治疗中将它们分离出来。”

paras.en: "That way you would be able to stimulate brown fat in people with normal blood pressure."
paras.zh: “这样你就能够刺激血压正常的人体内的棕色脂肪。”

paras.en: There are several caveats to sift through here. The association between blood pressure drugs and brown fat was identified in people, but the drug's ability to activate brown fat was demonstrated in mice, which are more reliant on brown fat than we are.
paras.zh: 这里有几个注意事项需要仔细检查。降血压药物与棕色脂肪之间的关联已在人体中得到证实，但该药物激活棕色脂肪的能力在小鼠身上得到了证实，小鼠比我们更依赖棕色脂肪。

paras.en: When it comes to the original database of medical records, all the participants had been diagnosed with cancer, and more than three-quarters were women, so future research needs to be expanded to include other groups of people.
paras.zh: 在原始病历数据库中，所有参与者都被诊断出患有癌症，其中超过四分之三是女性，因此未来的研究需要扩大到包括其他人群。

paras.en: All that said, it's a solid step towards understanding more about the benefits of brown fat and how it could be more readily activated. Each of the findings here is a foundation that other studies can build on.
paras.zh: 话虽如此，这是朝着更多地了解棕色脂肪的好处以及如何更容易地激活它迈出的坚实一步。这里的每一项发现都是其他研究可以建立的基础。

paras.en: "The unique reverse translational approach of this study, enabled by large clinical datasets and next-generation analytical tools, provides a much-needed clinical rationale for exploring brown adipose tissue as a therapeutic target in humans across a spectrum of diseases," says Griffin Rodgers, director of the NIH's National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, who wasn't involved in the research.
paras.zh: 美国国立卫生研究院国家糖尿病、消化和肾脏疾病研究所所长格里芬·罗杰斯（未参与这项研究）表示：“这项研究独特的反向转化方法，在大型临床数据集和下一代分析工具的支持下，为探索棕色脂肪组织作为人类多种疾病的治疗靶点提供了急需的临床原理。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Nature.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《自然》杂志上。

articles.title: Best of Both Worlds: 'Hybrid' Quantum Computers Could Be Just Around The Corner, Researchers Say
articles.author: Ivan Farkas

paras.en: For all their promise, quantum computers have a hard time modeling the interactions between the two families of building blocks that underlie our Universe – can you imagine a chef that struggles to describe how sugar and milk make cake?
paras.zh: 尽管量子计算机有很多承诺，但它很难对构成我们宇宙的两个构建模块家族之间的相互作用进行建模——你能想象一个厨师努力描述糖和牛奶如何制作蛋糕吗？

paras.en: But researchers may have found a way to overcome this challenge by modeling a theoretical 'hybrid' quantum computer that promises to combine the best of both worlds.
paras.zh: 但研究人员可能已经找到了一种方法来克服这一挑战，即对理论上的“混合”量子计算机进行建模，该计算机有望结合两个领域的优点。

paras.en: The fundamental particles that make up the cosmic cake of our existence are grouped as either fermions or bosons.
paras.zh: 构成我们存在的宇宙蛋糕的基本粒子分为费米子或玻色子。

paras.en: In simplest terms, fermions are particles of matter, including electrons and protons, and bosons include force-mediating particles, like the photons (light) that carry the electromagnetic force.
paras.zh: 简而言之，费米子是物质粒子，包括电子和质子，玻色子包括力介导粒子，例如携带电磁力的光子（光）。

paras.en: Quantum computers are great at modeling fermions, because they're more discrete, just like the qubits that power quantum computing.
paras.zh: 量子计算机非常擅长对费米子进行建模，因为它们更加离散，就像为量子计算提供动力的量子位一样。

paras.en: But bosons are tougher because they can occupy the same quantum state and 'overlap', meaning that one can have a quantum stack of infinite bosons.
paras.zh: 但玻色子更难，因为它们可以占据相同的量子态并“重叠”，这意味着人们可以拥有无​​限玻色子的量子堆栈。

paras.en: A new theoretical framework could bypass this issue and supercharge quantum computing, thanks to a new study from a team of physicists, engineers, and computer scientists, led by Eleanor Crane, a quantum computing lecturer at King's College London.
paras.zh: 伦敦国王学院量子计算讲师埃莉诺·克兰 (Eleanor Crane) 领导的物理学家、工程师和计算机科学家团队进行了一项新研究，一个新的理论框架可以绕过这个问题并增强量子计算的性能。
